**Ferdinand** "**Bongbong** " **Romualdez Marcos Jr.**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-3) (born September 13, 1957), commonly referred to by the initials **BBM** or **PBBM** , is a Filipino politician who has served as the 17th [president of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Philippines "President of the Philippines") since 2022.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-5) He is the second child and only son of 10th president [Ferdinand Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos "Ferdinand Marcos") and former first lady [Imelda Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imelda_Marcos "Imelda Marcos").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-6)
In 1980, Marcos was elected vice governor of [Ilocos Norte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilocos_Norte "Ilocos Norte"), running unopposed with the [Kilusang Bagong Lipunan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilusang_Bagong_Lipunan "Kilusang Bagong Lipunan") party of his father, who [was ruling the Philippines under martial law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_law_under_Ferdinand_Marcos "Martial law under Ferdinand Marcos") at the time.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Ellison2005-7) He then became [governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Ilocos_Norte "Governor of Ilocos Norte") in 1983, holding that office until his family was ousted from power by the [People Power Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_Power_Revolution "People Power Revolution") and fled into exile in Hawaii in February 1986. After the death of his father in 1989, President [Corazon Aquino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corazon_Aquino "Corazon Aquino") allowed his family to return to the Philippines to face various charges; in October 1991, he became the first Marcos to return since the revolution. Marcos and his mother, Imelda, are currently facing arrest in the United States for defying a court order to pay [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")353 million ([₱](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_peso "Philippine peso")17,385,250,000 in 2025) in restitution to [human rights abuse victims during his father's dictatorship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights_abuses_of_the_Marcos_dictatorship "Human rights abuses of the Marcos dictatorship").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-bongbongCantVisitUSA-8) As president, however, he may enter the United States by virtue of diplomatic immunity.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-9)
Marcos was elected as the [representative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Representatives_of_the_Philippines "House of Representatives of the Philippines") of [Ilocos Norte's second district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilocos_Norte's_2nd_congressional_district "Ilocos Norte's 2nd congressional district"), serving from 1992 to 1995. He was elected governor again in 1998. After nine years, he returned to his previous position as representative from 2007 to 2010, before entering the [Senate of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_of_the_Philippines "Senate of the Philippines") under the [Nacionalista Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nacionalista_Party "Nacionalista Party") for a single term from 2010 to 2016.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-10) Marcos unsuccessfully ran for [vice president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_Philippines "Vice President of the Philippines") in the [2016 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Philippine_general_election "2016 Philippine general election"), narrowly losing to [Camarines Sur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camarines_Sur's_3rd_congressional_district "Camarines Sur's 3rd congressional district") representative [Leni Robredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leni_Robredo "Leni Robredo"). Marcos contested the result at the [Presidential Electoral Tribunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Electoral_Tribunal "Presidential Electoral Tribunal") but his electoral protest was unanimously dismissed in 2021 after the pilot recount resulted in Robredo widening her lead by 15,093 additional votes.
Marcos ran for president in the [2022 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Philippine_presidential_election "2022 Philippine presidential election") under the [Partido Federal ng Pilipinas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partido_Federal_ng_Pilipinas "Partido Federal ng Pilipinas"),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-11) which he won by a landslide with nearly 59% of the vote.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Verizon-2022-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Morales-2022-13) During his campaign, he refrained from participating in presidential debates. Although President [Rodrigo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte "Rodrigo Duterte") had expressed criticisms of Marcos as a "weak leader", Duterte's daughter [Sara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Duterte "Sara Duterte") ran as Marcos' running mate and won a majority of the votes, with their [UniTeam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UniTeam "UniTeam") coalition being credited for their resounding electoral success. His win was the largest since [1981](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_Philippine_presidential_election_and_referendum "1981 Philippine presidential election and referendum"), when his father won 88% of the votes due to a boycott by the opposition.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-15)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-16) His presidential campaign received criticism from fact-checkers and disinformation scholars for being driven by historical negationism aimed at [rehabilitating the Marcos brand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_distortion_regarding_Ferdinand_Marcos "Historical distortion regarding Ferdinand Marcos") and smearing his rivals.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-filipinosFallFakeHistory-17)
As president, Marcos concurrently served as the [Secretary of Agriculture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_Agriculture_\(Philippines\) "Secretary of Agriculture \(Philippines\)") in his initial 16 months. He continued the [Build! Build! Build!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Build!_Build!_Build! "Build! Build! Build!") infrastructure program of President Duterte through his own program called "[Build Better More](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Build_Better_More "Build Better More")". Foreign policy has been characterized by efforts to reestablish closer ties with the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States"), an abrupt shift from the China-oriented policies of the Duterte administration. Amidst China's increased [territorial encroachment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_reactions_to_China's_maritime_activities_in_the_South_China_Sea#The_Philippines "Regional reactions to China's maritime activities in the South China Sea") in the maritime area within the [West Philippine Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Philippine_Sea "West Philippine Sea") that has led to standoffs with Filipino vessels, Marcos has repeatedly affirmed Philippine jurisdiction over the area, stating in 2023 that "This country will not lose an inch of its territory".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-18) In 2024, Marcos banned [Philippine offshore gaming operators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_offshore_gaming_operator "Philippine offshore gaming operator") that had proliferated under the previous administration, while Vice President [Sara Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Duterte "Sara Duterte") resigned from his cabinet amidst a growing rift in the [Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcos_family "Marcos family") and [Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duterte_family "Duterte family") political families. The year 2025 was marked by [controversy over the national budget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Appropriations_Act_of_2025 "General Appropriations Act of 2025"), the [impeachment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_impeachment_of_Sara_Duterte "First impeachment of Sara Duterte") of Vice President Duterte, the [arrest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrest_of_Rodrigo_Duterte "Arrest of Rodrigo Duterte") of former president Rodrigo Duterte, and a [massive infrastructure corruption scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flood_control_projects_controversy_in_the_Philippines "Flood control projects controversy in the Philippines") he had initially publicized and denounced.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-19)
## Early life and education
Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr. was born on September 13, 1957 to [Ferdinand Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos "Ferdinand Marcos") and [Imelda Romualdez Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imelda_Marcos "Imelda Marcos"), at a hospital in [Santa Mesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Mesa "Santa Mesa"), Manila, Philippines, which became known as the [Our Lady of Lourdes Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Lady_of_Lourdes_Hospital_\(Manila\) "Our Lady of Lourdes Hospital \(Manila\)") the following year.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-22) At the time of his birth, his father Ferdinand was the representative for the [second district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilocos_Norte's_2nd_congressional_district "Ilocos Norte's 2nd congressional district") of [Ilocos Norte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilocos_Norte "Ilocos Norte"), and became a senator two years later. His godfathers include the "[Marcos cronies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcos_cronies "Marcos cronies")" [Eduardo "Danding" Cojuangco Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danding_Cojuangco "Danding Cojuangco")[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Seagrave1988-23): 286  and [Jose Yao Campos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_Yao_Campos "Jose Yao Campos").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-FloresWilsonLee20060508-24)
### Education
Marcos first studied at the [Institución Teresiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Pedro_Poveda_College "Saint Pedro Poveda College") in [Quezon City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quezon_City "Quezon City") and [La Salle Green Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Salle_Green_Hills "La Salle Green Hills") in [Mandaluyong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandaluyong "Mandaluyong"), where he obtained his kindergarten and elementary education, respectively.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-SenateGovPH-Bongbong-25)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-26)
In 1970, Marcos was sent to England where he lived and studied at [Worth School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worth_School "Worth School"), an all-boys [Benedictine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedictine "Benedictine") institution in [West Sussex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Sussex "West Sussex").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-SydneyMorningHerald20121124-27)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Legaspi-28) He was studying there when his father [declared](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proclamation_1081 "Proclamation 1081") [martial law throughout the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_law_under_Ferdinand_Marcos "Martial law under Ferdinand Marcos") in 1972.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-SydneyMorningHerald20121124-27)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Legaspi-28)
Marcos attended the [Center for Research and Communication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Asia_and_the_Pacific "University of Asia and the Pacific"), where he took a special diploma course in economics, but did not finish.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_admits_not_finishing_%E2%80%98special_diploma%E2%80%99_course_in_UA&P-29)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_admits_not_finishing_UA&P_certificate_program-30) He then enrolled at [St Edmund Hall, Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Edmund_Hall,_Oxford "St Edmund Hall, Oxford"), to study [philosophy, politics and economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy,_politics_and_economics "Philosophy, politics and economics") (PPE). Despite his false claims that he graduated with a bachelor of arts in PPE,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-31) he did not obtain such a degree.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-rappler.com-32)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-33)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-cnnphilippines.com-34) Marcos passed philosophy, but failed economics, and failed politics twice, making him ineligible for graduation.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-kasarinlan1-35)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-iTutoredBongbong-36) Instead, he received a special diploma in social studies,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-cnnphilippines.com-34) which was awarded mainly to non-graduates and is currently no longer offered by the university.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-rappler.com-32)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-documentsBongbongEducationOxford-37) Marcos still falsely claims that he obtained a degree from the University of Oxford despite the university confirming in 2015 that Marcos did not finish his degree.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-oxfordNoDegree-38)
Marcos enrolled in the master's in [business administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_Administration "Business Administration") program at the [Wharton School of Business, University of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wharton_School_of_the_University_of_Pennsylvania "Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania"), in [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia"), United States, which he failed to complete. Marcos asserts that he withdrew from the program after his election to be Vice Governor of Ilocos Norte in 1980.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-39) The [Presidential Commission on Good Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Commission_on_Good_Government "Presidential Commission on Good Government") later reported that his tuition, his US$10,000 (₱492,500 in 2025) monthly allowance, and the estate he lived in while studying at Wharton, were paid using funds that could be traced partly to the intelligence funds of the Office of the President, and partly to some of the fifteen bank accounts that the Marcoses had secretly opened in the US under assumed names.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Manapat2020-40)
### Early public roles
See also: [Iginuhit ng Tadhana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iginuhit_ng_Tadhana "Iginuhit ng Tadhana") and [The Beatles' 1966 tour of Germany, Japan and the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles'_1966_tour_of_Germany,_Japan_and_the_Philippines "The Beatles' 1966 tour of Germany, Japan and the Philippines")
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/Meeting_of_the_Marcoses_and_the_Nixons_in_1969_at_the_Malaca%C3%B1ang_Palace.jpg/250px-Meeting_of_the_Marcoses_and_the_Nixons_in_1969_at_the_Malaca%C3%B1ang_Palace.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Meeting_of_the_Marcoses_and_the_Nixons_in_1969_at_the_Malaca%C3%B1ang_Palace.jpg)Ferdinand and Imelda Marcos meeting with United States president [Richard Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon"), shown holding Bongbong, in 1969
Marcos was thrust into the national limelight as early as when he was three years old, and the scrutiny became even more intense when his father first ran for President of the Philippines in 1965,[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Lo20100413-41) when he was eight years old.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-SydneyMorningHerald20121124-27)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Legaspi-28)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Seagrave1988-23)
During his father's 1965 campaign, Marcos played himself in the [Sampaguita Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sampaguita_Pictures "Sampaguita Pictures") film _[Iginuhit ng Tadhana (The Ferdinand E. Marcos Story)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iginuhit_ng_Tadhana_\(The_Ferdinand_E._Marcos_Story\) "Iginuhit ng Tadhana \(The Ferdinand E. Marcos Story\)")_ , a biopic based on the novel _For Every Tear a Victory_.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Gomez150826-42)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Lo20100413-41) The young Marcos was portrayed giving a speech towards the end of the film, in which he says that he would like to be a politician when he grows up.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Geronimo20151012-43) The public relations value of the film is credited for having helped the elder Marcos win the [1965 Philippine elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1965_Philippine_presidential_election "1965 Philippine presidential election").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Garcia2016-44)
A young Bongbong Marcos and his sister Imee played a small role in the controversial "[Manila incident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles'_1966_tour_of_Germany,_Japan_and_the_Philippines#Philippines "The Beatles' 1966 tour of Germany, Japan and the Philippines")" of [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") in July 1966, just six months after their father assumed the presidency.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-OliverXAReyes20170524-45)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-46): 200  Bongbong and Imee were among 400 children whom their mother Imelda brought to Malacañang Palace for a reception in which they expected the Beatles to show up.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-OliverXAReyes20170524-45) The four band members claimed not to know about the event, and refused to attend.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-OliverXAReyes20170524-45)
As the event went on without them, the Marcos children were interviewed. Bongbong, referring to the group's long hair, was quoted saying "I'd like to pounce on the Beatles and cut off their hair! Don't anybody dare me to do anything, because I'll do it, just to see how game the Beatles are."[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-OliverXAReyes20170524-45) Imee, meantime, was quoted saying "There is only one song I like from the Beatles, and it's [Run for Your Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Run_for_Your_Life_\(Beatles_song\) "Run for Your Life \(Beatles song\)")."[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-OliverXAReyes20170524-45)—a quote which media later associated with the way the Beatles scrambled out of Manila, receiving rough treatment at [Manila International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila_International_Airport "Manila International Airport").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-OliverXAReyes20170524-45)
Beatles lead guitarist [George Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Harrison "George Harrison") later accused the Marcoses of inciting Filipinos to mob the band as they tried to leave the country for not showing up at the reception, saying in a 1986 interview at [NBC's _Today Show_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Today_\(American_TV_program\) "Today \(American TV program\)") that the Marcoses "tried to kill [them]."[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-SalvaESQ2021-47)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Twit-48) Harrison said that their plane was not allowed to leave Manila until their manager, [Brian Epstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Epstein "Brian Epstein"), refunded the concert ticket money.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-SalvaESQ2021-47)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Twit-48)
The _[Manila Bulletin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila_Bulletin "Manila Bulletin")_ reported in 2015 that Marcos had once invited Beatles drummer [Ringo Starr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ringo_Starr "Ringo Starr") to return to the Philippines "to bring closure" to the incident.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-25_things-49) The incident was brought up in the media again after a 2021 interview between Marcos and actress [Toni Gonzaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toni_Gonzaga "Toni Gonzaga"), when he was asked about which musicians he idolized, and he casually mentioned that he was friends with [Mick Jagger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Jagger "Mick Jagger") of [the Rolling Stones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rolling_Stones "The Rolling Stones") and members of the Beatles.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-SalvaESQ2021-47)
Marcos was still a minor in 1972 [when martial law was declared](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_law_under_Ferdinand_Marcos "Martial law under Ferdinand Marcos"). Marcos turned 18 in 1975[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-mlchroniclesaccountable-50)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-EricaSauler20160205-51)—a year after he graduated from Worth School.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-52)
## Roles in the Marcos regime
### Vice governorship and governorship in Ilocos Norte
Marcos's first formal role in a political office came with his election as Vice Governor of Ilocos Norte (1980–1983) at the age of 22.  On March 23, 1983, he was installed as the [Governor of Ilocos Norte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Ilocos_Norte "Governor of Ilocos Norte"), replacing his aunt Elizabeth Marcos-Keon, who had resigned from the post for health reasons.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-53) In 1983, he led a group of young Filipino leaders on a 10-day diplomatic mission to China to mark the tenth anniversary of [Philippine–Chinese relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China%E2%80%93Philippines_relations "China–Philippines relations").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-54) He stayed in office until the [People Power Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_Power_Revolution "People Power Revolution") in 1986.
During Marcos's term, at least two [extrajudicial killings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extrajudicial_killings_and_forced_disappearances_in_the_Philippines "Extrajudicial killings and forced disappearances in the Philippines") took place in Ilocos Norte, as documented by the Martial Law Victims Association of Ilocos Norte (MLVAIN).[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Cornelio20160415-55)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-56)
### Chairmanship of PHILCOMSAT Board
Marcos was appointed by his father to be chairman of the board of the [Philippine Communications Satellite Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Communications_Satellite_Corporation "Philippine Communications Satellite Corporation") (PHILCOMSAT) in early 1985.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-JamainePunzalan20161125-57) In a prominent example of what Finance Minister [Jaime Ongpin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaime_Ongpin "Jaime Ongpin") later branded "[crony capitalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crony_capitalism "Crony capitalism")", the Marcos administration had sold its majority shares to [Marcos cronies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcos_cronies "Marcos cronies") such as [Roberto S. Benedicto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_S._Benedicto "Roberto S. Benedicto"),[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Scott1986-58) [Manuel H. Nieto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cronies_of_Ferdinand_Marcos "Cronies of Ferdinand Marcos"),[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Scott1986-58) [Jose Yao Campos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_Yao_Campos "Jose Yao Campos"),[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Butterfield19860330-59) and [Rolando Gapud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolando_Gapud "Rolando Gapud")[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Butterfield19860330-59) in 1982, despite being very profitable because of its role as the sole agent for the Philippines' link to global satellite network Intelsat.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Scott1986-58)
President Marcos acquired a 39.9% share in the company, through front companies under Campos and Gapud.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Butterfield19860330-59) This allowed President Marcos to appoint his son as the chairman of the Philcomsat board in early 1985, allowing the young Marcos to draw a monthly salary "ranging from US$9,700 to US$97,000"[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-JamainePunzalan20161125-57)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Scott1986-58) (₱477,725 to ₱4,777,250 in 2025) despite rarely visiting the office and having no duties there.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Scott1986-58)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-JamainePunzalan20161125-57) PHILCOMSAT was one of five telecommunications firms sequestered by the Philippine government in 1986.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Scott1986-58)
### Ill-gotten Marcos family wealth
Main article: [Unexplained wealth of the Marcos family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unexplained_wealth_of_the_Marcos_family "Unexplained wealth of the Marcos family")
After the Marcos family went into exile in 1986, the [Presidential Commission on Good Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Commission_on_Good_Government "Presidential Commission on Good Government") found that the three Marcos children benefited significantly[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Manapat2020-40)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-JamainePunzalan20161125-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Garcia2106-60) from what the [Supreme Court of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_Philippines "Supreme Court of the Philippines") defined as "ill-gotten wealth" of the Marcos family.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-scImeldaMarcosvsRP-61)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-TiongsonMayrina-62)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Salonga2000-63)
Aside from the tuition, US$10,000 (₱492,500 in 2025) monthly allowance, and the estates used by Marcos Jr. and Imee Marcos during their respective studies at Wharton and Princeton,[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Manapat2020-40) each of the Marcos children was assigned a [mansion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcos_mansions "Marcos mansions") in the Metro Manila area, as well as in [Baguio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baguio "Baguio"), the Philippines' designated summer capital.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Manapat2020-40) Properties specifically said to have been given to Marcos Jr. included the Wigwam House compound on Outlook Drive in Baguio[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Manapat2020-40) and the Seaside Mansion Compound in [Parañaque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Para%C3%B1aque "Parañaque").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Manapat2020-40)
In addition, by the time their father was ousted from power in 1986, both Marcos Jr. and Imee held key posts in the Marcos administration.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-JamainePunzalan20161125-57) Imee was already 30 when she was appointed as the national head of the Kabataang Barangay in the late 1970s,[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-JamainePunzalan20161125-57) and Marcos Jr. was in his 20s when he took up the vice-gubernatorial post for the province of Ilocos Norte in 1980, and then became governor of that province from 1983 until the Marcos family was ousted from Malacañang in 1986.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-JamainePunzalan20161125-57)
### As an Officer of the Philippine Constabulary
Marcos Jr. was commissioned as a Second Lieutenant in the [Philippine Constabulary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Constabulary "Philippine Constabulary") Reserve in 1978, as a member of the Presidential Security Command, while serving as a special presidential assistant for his father. He had also undergone a six-month officer course at the Philippine Marine Training Center.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-64)
## EDSA revolution and exile (1986–1991)
Further information: [People Power Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_Power_Revolution "People Power Revolution")
During the last days of the 1986 [People Power Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_Power_Revolution "People Power Revolution"), Bongbong Marcos, dressed in combat fatigues to project his warlike stance,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-usSet5Conditions-65) pushed his father [Ferdinand Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos "Ferdinand Marcos") to give the order to his remaining troops to attack and blow up [Camp Crame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Crame "Camp Crame") despite the presence of hundreds of thousands of civilians there. The elder Marcos did not follow his son's urgings.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-fmLastDayPalace-66)
Fearful of a scenario in which Marcos's presence in the Philippines would lead to a civil war,[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-StuartSantiago1995-67) the [Reagan administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reagan_administration "Reagan administration") withdrew its support for the Marcos government, and flew Marcos and a party of about 80 individuals[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-DavidHolley19860228-68) – the extended Marcos family and a number of close associates[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-APmanifest19860311-69) – from the Philippines to Hawaii despite Ferdinand Marcos's objections.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-StuartSantiago1995-67) Bongbong Marcos and his family were on the flight with his parents.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-DavidHolley19860227-70)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-71)
Soon after arriving in Hawaii, the younger Marcos participated in an attempt to withdraw US$200 million (₱9,849,999,999.96 in 2025) from a [secret family bank account](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_secrecy "Bank secrecy") with [Credit Suisse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Credit_Suisse "Credit Suisse") in Switzerland,[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-SCMP2011-72) an act which eventually led to the Swiss government freezing the Marcoses' bank accounts in late March that year.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-WaPoSwissFreeze-73)
The Marcoses initially stayed at [Hickam Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hickam_Air_Force_Base "Hickam Air Force Base") at the expense of the U.S. government. A month after arriving in [Honolulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu "Honolulu"), they moved into a pair of residences in [Makiki Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makiki_Heights "Makiki Heights"), Honolulu, which were registered to [Marcos cronies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcos_cronies "Marcos cronies") [Antonio Floirendo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Floirendo "Antonio Floirendo") and Bienvenido and Gliceria Tantoco.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-DavidHolley19860228-68)
Ferdinand Marcos eventually died in exile three years later, in 1989,[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Richburg&Branigin19890929-74) with Marcos Jr. being the only family member present at his father's deathbed.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Aruiza1991-75)
## Return to the Philippines; political career (1991–2022)
In the early 1990s, President [Corazon Aquino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corazon_Aquino "Corazon Aquino") permitted the return of the remaining members of the Marcos family to the Philippines to face various charges.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-SethMydans19911104-76) Bongbong Marcos flew on a private plane from Singapore to the Philippines and landed in [Laoag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laoag "Laoag"), [Ilocos Norte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilocos_Norte "Ilocos Norte") on October 31, 1991, becoming the first Marcos family member to return to the Philippines since 1986; his mother Imelda followed suit four days later.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-77)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-78)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-79) He soon sought political office, beginning in the family's traditional [fiefdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiefdom "Fiefdom") in Ilocos Norte.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-80)
### House of Representatives, first term
Further information: [1992 Philippine House of Representatives elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Philippine_House_of_Representatives_elections "1992 Philippine House of Representatives elections")
Marcos ran for and was elected representative of the [second district of Ilocos Norte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilocos_Norte's_2nd_congressional_district "Ilocos Norte's 2nd congressional district") to the [Philippine House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Representatives_of_the_Philippines "House of Representatives of the Philippines") (1992–1995).[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-81) When his mother, Imelda Marcos, ran for president in the same election, he decided against supporting her candidacy, and instead expressed support for his godfather Danding Cojuangco.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-82) During his term, Marcos was the author of 29 House bills and co-author of 90 more, which includes those that paved the way for the creation of the [Department of Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Energy_\(Philippines\) "Department of Energy \(Philippines\)") and the [National Youth Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Youth_Commission_\(Philippines\) "National Youth Commission \(Philippines\)").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bueza-2015-83) He also allocated most of his Countryside Development Fund (CDF) to organizing the cooperatives of teachers and farmers in his home province.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-84)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-About_Bongbong_Marcos-85)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] In October 1992, he led a group of ten representatives in attending the first sports summit in the Philippines, held in [Baguio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baguio "Baguio").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-86) In late 1994, he was made president of the [Kilusang Bagong Lipunan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilusang_Bagong_Lipunan "Kilusang Bagong Lipunan") party, which is known for its support for the Marcos regime.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-87)
[In 1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_Philippine_Senate_election "1995 Philippine Senate election"), Marcos ran for the Senate under the [NPC-led coalition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationalist_People's_Coalition "Nationalist People's Coalition") but lost, placing only 16th.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-88)
#### Compromise deal attempt
In 1995, Bongbong Marcos pushed a deal to allow the Marcos family to keep a quarter of the estimated US$2 billion to US$10 billion (₱98,499,999,999.61 to ₱492,499,999,998.03 in 2025) that the Philippine government had still not recovered from them, on the condition that all civil cases be dropped – a deal that was eventually struck down by the Philippines' Supreme Court.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-SCMP2011-72)
### Ilocos Norte governor, second stint
Having previously served as Ilocos Norte governor from 1983 to 1986, Marcos was again elected as governor of Ilocos Norte in 1998, running against his father's closest friend and ally, [Roque Ablan Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roque_Ablan_Jr. "Roque Ablan Jr.") He served for three consecutive terms ending in 2007.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-89)
### House of Representatives, second term
In 2007, Marcos ran unopposed for the congressional seat previously held by his older sister [Imee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imee_Marcos "Imee Marcos").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-90) He was then appointed as deputy minority leader of the House of Representatives. During this term, Marcos supported the passage of the Philippine Archipelagic Baselines Law, or Republic Act No. 9522.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-91) He also wrote his own version of the law, but the bill only remained in the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bueza-2015-83)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-92) He also promoted the Republic Act No. 9502 (Universally Accessible Cheaper and Quality Medicines Act) which was enacted on 2009.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-93)
### Senate career
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Ferdinand_Marcos_Jr._during_a_Kapihan_sa_Senado_forum.jpg/250px-Ferdinand_Marcos_Jr._during_a_Kapihan_sa_Senado_forum.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ferdinand_Marcos_Jr._during_a_Kapihan_sa_Senado_forum.jpg)Senator Marcos during a forum in June 2014 [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Bongbong_Marcos.jpg/250px-Bongbong_Marcos.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bongbong_Marcos.jpg)Portrait during his stint as senator
Further information: [2010 Philippine Senate election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Philippine_Senate_election "2010 Philippine Senate election")
Marcos made a second attempt for the Senate in [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Philippine_general_election "2010 Philippine general election"). On November 20, 2009, the KBL forged an alliance with the [Nacionalista Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nacionalista_Party "Nacionalista Party") (NP) between Marcos and NP chair Senator [Manny Villar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manny_Villar "Manny Villar") at the [Laurel House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_P._Laurel_Residence "Jose P. Laurel Residence") in [Mandaluyong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandaluyong "Mandaluyong"). Marcos became a guest senatorial candidate of the NP through this alliance.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Philstar_NP_KBL-94) Marcos was later removed as a member by the KBL National Executive Committee on November 23, 2009.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-95) As such, the NP broke its alliance with the KBL due to internal conflicts within the party, however Marcos remained part of the NP senatorial lineup.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Philstar_NP_KBL-94) He was proclaimed as one of the winning senatorial candidates of the [2010 senate elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Philippine_Senate_election "2010 Philippine Senate election"). He took office on June 30, 2010.
In the [15th Congress (2010–2013)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15th_Congress_of_the_Philippines "15th Congress of the Philippines"), Marcos authored 34 Senate bills. He also co-authored 17 bills of which seven were enacted into law[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bueza-2015-83) – most notably the Anti-Drunk and Drugged Driving Act whose principal author was Senator [Vicente Sotto III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vicente_Sotto_III "Vicente Sotto III"); the [Cybercrime Prevention Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cybercrime_Prevention_Act_of_2012 "Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012") whose principal author was Senator [Edgardo Angara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgardo_Angara "Edgardo Angara"); and the Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons and the National Health Insurance Acts, both of which were principally authored by Senator [Loren Legarda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loren_Legarda "Loren Legarda").
[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Senate_of_the_Philippines_-_16th_Congress_-_Session_No._69_\(May_5,_2015\)_-_Bongbong_Marcos_and_General_Trias_City_Charter.webm "Play video")[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Senate_of_the_Philippines_-_16th_Congress_-_Session_No._69_\(May_5,_2015\)_-_Bongbong_Marcos_and_General_Trias_City_Charter.webm)Marcos delivering a sponsorship speech on the charter of the City of [General Trias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Trias "General Trias") in 2015.
In the [16th Congress (2013–2016)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16th_Congress_of_the_Philippines "16th Congress of the Philippines"), Marcos filed 52 bills, of which 28 were refiled from the 15th Congress. One of them was enacted into law: Senate Bill No. 1186, which sought the postponement of the [2013 Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Philippine_barangay_elections "2013 Philippine barangay elections"), was enacted as Republic Act No. 10632 on October 3, 2013.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bueza-2015-83)
Marcos also co-authored 4 Senate bills in the 16th Congress. One of them, Senate Bill No. 712 which was principally authored by [Ralph Recto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Recto "Ralph Recto"), was enacted as Republic Act No. 10645, the Expanded Senior Citizens Act of 2010.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bueza-2015-83)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-96)
He was the chair of the Senate committees on urban planning, housing and resettlement, local government, and public works.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-97) He also chaired the oversight committee on the [Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_Region_in_Muslim_Mindanao "Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao") Organic Act, the congressional oversight panel on the Special Purpose Vehicle Act, and a select oversight committee on [barangay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barangay "Barangay") affairs.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-SenateGovPH-Bongbong-25)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bueza-2015-83)
#### 2014 pork barrel scam
In 2014, Bongbong Marcos was implicated by [Janet Lim Napoles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Lim_Napoles "Janet Lim Napoles")[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-20senatorsPDAF-98) and Benhur Luy[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-25Senators-99) in the [Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) Pork Barrel scam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priority_Development_Assistance_Fund_scam "Priority Development Assistance Fund scam") through agent Catherine Mae "Maya" Santos.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-affidavitNapoles-100) He allegedly channeled ₱100 million through 4 fake [NGOs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-governmental_organization "Non-governmental organization") linked with Napoles.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-abadShouldHaveChecked-101) Marcos claimed that the large amounts of money was released by the budget department without his knowledge and that his signatures were forged.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-MarcosFundMisuse-102) In connection to the PDAF scam, Marcos was also sued for plunder by iBalik ang Bilyones ng Mamamayan (iBBM), an alliance of youth organizations. The group cited Luy's digital files, which showed bogus NGOs with shady or non-existent offices.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-bongbongMarcosPlunder-103)
#### 2016 Commission on Audit suit
In 2016, Marcos was also sued for _plunder_ for funneling ₱205 million of his PDAF via 9 special allotment release orders (SARO) to the following bogus foundations from October 2011 to January 2013, according to Luy's digital files:[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-bongbongMarcosPlunder-103)
  * Social Development Program for Farmers Foundation (SDPFFI) – ₱15 million
  * Countrywide Agri and Rural Economic Development Foundation (CARED) – ₱35 million
  * People's Organization for Progress and Development Foundation (POPDFI) – ₱40 million
  * Health Education Assistance Resettlement Training Services (HEARTS) – ₱10 million
  * Kaupdanan Para Sa Mangunguma Foundation (KMFI) – ₱20 million
  * National Livelihood Development Corporation (NLDC) – ₱100 million


These NGOs were found by the [Commission on Audit (COA)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_on_Audit_of_the_Philippines "Commission on Audit of the Philippines") as bogus with shady or non-existent offices.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-bongbongMarcosPlunder-103)
### 2016 vice presidential campaign
Further information: [2016 Philippine presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Philippine_presidential_election "2016 Philippine presidential election")
Main article: [Miriam Defensor Santiago 2016 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miriam_Defensor_Santiago_2016_presidential_campaign "Miriam Defensor Santiago 2016 presidential campaign")
![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/Wikiquote-logo.svg/40px-Wikiquote-logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)
Wikiquote has quotations related to _**[Bongbong Marcos's 2016 Vice Presidential campaign](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Bongbong%20Marcos "q:Bongbong Marcos")**_.
On October 5, 2015, Marcos announced via his website that he would run for [Vice President of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_Philippines "Vice President of the Philippines") in the [2016 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Philippine_general_election "2016 Philippine general election"), stating "I have decided to run for vice president in the May 2016 elections."[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-CNN_Philippines_2015-10-05-104)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-105) Marcos ran as an independent candidate.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-106) Prior to his announcement, he had declined an invitation by presidential candidate, Vice President [Jejomar Binay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jejomar_Binay "Jejomar Binay"), to become his running mate.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-107) On October 15, 2015, presidential candidate [Miriam Defensor Santiago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miriam_Defensor_Santiago "Miriam Defensor Santiago") confirmed that Marcos would serve as her running mate.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-108)
Marcos placed second in the tightly contested vice presidential race, losing to [Camarines Sur's 3rd district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camarines_Sur's_3rd_congressional_district "Camarines Sur's 3rd congressional district") representative [Leni Robredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leni_Robredo "Leni Robredo"), who won by a margin of 263,473 votes,[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-slim_margin_1-109)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-slim_margin_2-110) one of the closest since [Fernando Lopez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Lopez "Fernando Lopez")'s victory in the 1965 vice presidential election.
#### Election results protest
Main article: [2016 Philippine presidential election § Electoral protest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Philippine_presidential_election#Electoral_protest "2016 Philippine presidential election")
Marcos challenged the results of the election, lodging an electoral protest against Leni Robredo on June 29, 2016, the day before Robredo's oathtaking.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-VeraFilesPETTimeline-111)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-112) President [Rodrigo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte "Rodrigo Duterte") has stated several times that he would resign if Marcos would be his successor instead of Vice President Leni Robredo.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-BernadetteNicolas20180816-113)
A recount began in April 2018, covering polling precincts in Iloilo and Camarines Sur, which were areas handpicked by Marcos's camp. In October 2019, the tribunal found that Robredo's lead grew by around 15,000 votes – a total of 278,566 votes from Robredo's original lead of 263,473 votes – after a recount of ballots from the 5,415 clustered precincts in Marcos's identified pilot provinces.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-114) On February 16, 2021, the [Presidential Electoral Tribunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Electoral_Tribunal "Presidential Electoral Tribunal") (PET) unanimously dismissed Bongbong Marcos's electoral protest against Leni Robredo.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-PETdismissalSCMP-115)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-PETdismissalCNN-116)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-PETdecisionABSCBN-117)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-TetchTorresTupasPETDecision-118)
### 2022 presidential campaign and election
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/Marcos_Duterte-Carpio_caravan_in_Quezon_City.jpg/250px-Marcos_Duterte-Carpio_caravan_in_Quezon_City.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Marcos_Duterte-Carpio_caravan_in_Quezon_City.jpg)Marcos (center) and his running mate [Sara Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Duterte "Sara Duterte") during a grand caravan in [Quezon City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quezon_City "Quezon City") in December 2021
Further information: [2022 Philippine presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Philippine_presidential_election "2022 Philippine presidential election")
Main article: [Bongbong Marcos 2022 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos_2022_presidential_campaign "Bongbong Marcos 2022 presidential campaign")
Marcos officially launched his campaign for [president of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Philippines "President of the Philippines") on October 5, 2021, through a video post on Facebook and YouTube.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-119)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-120) An interview with his wife Liza Marcos revealed that he decided to run for president while watching the film _[Ant-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant-Man_\(film\) "Ant-Man \(film\)")_ ,[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-cnnAntmanPresidentialRun-121)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-inquirerAntmanPresidentialRun-122) though Marcos admitted that he could not recall this moment.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-123) He ran under the banner of the [Partido Federal ng Pilipinas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partido_Federal_ng_Pilipinas "Partido Federal ng Pilipinas") party, assuming chairmanship of the party on the same day,[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-CNN-124) while also being endorsed by his former party, the [Kilusang Bagong Lipunan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilusang_Bagong_Lipunan "Kilusang Bagong Lipunan").[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-125) He was endorsed by controversial religious group [Iglesia ni Cristo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iglesia_ni_Cristo "Iglesia ni Cristo") (INC).[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-126)
Marcos filed his certificate of candidacy before the [Commission on Elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_on_Elections_\(Philippines\) "Commission on Elections \(Philippines\)") the following day.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-127) On November 16, Marcos announced his running mate to be [Davao City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davao_City "Davao City") mayor [Sara Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Duterte "Sara Duterte"), daughter of President [Rodrigo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte "Rodrigo Duterte").[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-INQtandem-128) Under the campaign theme of unity, Marcos and Duterte's alliance was given the name "[UniTeam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UniTeam "UniTeam")".[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-INQtandem-128)
Seven petitions were filed against Marcos's presidential bid.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-CNNPH-Petitions-129)[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-130) Three petitions aimed to cancel his certificate of candidacy (COC), one petition aimed to declare Marcos a [nuisance candidate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuisance_candidate "Nuisance candidate"), and three petitions aimed to disqualify him. Most of the petitions were based on Marcos's [1995 conviction for failing to file tax returns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#1995_tax_case_conviction). Three disqualification petitions were consolidated and raffled to the commission's first division, while three other petitions were handed to the second division.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-CNNPH-Petitions-129)[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bordey-2021-131)
The final petition was handed to the first division. Marcos dismissed the petitions as nuisance petitions with no legal basis and propaganda against him.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-132) On May 16 and 18, 2022, respectively, [two of the petitions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_petitions_to_nullify_Bongbong_Marcos'_candidacy_in_the_2022_Philippine_presidential_election "Supreme Court petitions to nullify Bongbong Marcos' candidacy in the 2022 Philippine presidential election") were filed at the Supreme Court.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-133)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-134) The consolidated petitions were dismissed by the Court on June 28.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-135)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/2022_Provincial_Results_Presidential_Simplified.png/250px-2022_Provincial_Results_Presidential_Simplified.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2022_Provincial_Results_Presidential_Simplified.png)Marcos won in 64 out of 81 provinces in the [2022 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Philippine_presidential_election "2022 Philippine presidential election").[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-136)
Marcos regularly maintained a wide lead in presidential surveys throughout the months leading up to the May 2022 election;[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-137)[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-138) he was the first presidential candidate in the country to attain poll ratings of over 50% from surveys conducted by [Pulse Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulse_Asia "Pulse Asia") since it began polling in 1999.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-139) His refrainment from attending all but one of the presidential debates during the campaign season was widely criticized.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-140)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-141)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-142)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-143)
In a joint session of the [18th Congress of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/18th_Congress_of_the_Philippines "18th Congress of the Philippines"), overseen by Senate President [Tito Sotto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tito_Sotto "Tito Sotto") and [House Speaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speaker_of_the_House_of_Representatives_of_the_Philippines "Speaker of the House of Representatives of the Philippines") [Lord Allan Velasco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Allan_Velasco "Lord Allan Velasco") and stated by Senate Majority Leader [Migz Zubiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Migz_Zubiri "Migz Zubiri") and Majority Floor Leader [Martin Romualdez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Romualdez "Martin Romualdez"), Marcos was proclaimed the [president-elect of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President-elect_of_the_Philippines "President-elect of the Philippines") on May 25, 2022, alongside his running-mate, Vice-President-elect [Sara Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Duterte "Sara Duterte"). Marcos received 31,629,783 votes, or 58.77% of the total votes cast, about 16.5 million votes ahead of his closest rival, Vice President [Leni Robredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leni_Robredo "Leni Robredo"), who received over 15 million votes.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-144)
He became the first presidential candidate to be elected by a majority since the establishment of the Fifth Republic in [1986](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Philippine_presidential_election "1986 Philippine presidential election").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Verizon-2022-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Morales-2022-13)[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-145) According to analysts, Marcos, together with Sara Duterte, "inherited" Rodrigo Duterte's popularity when they both won landslides in the election.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-146) Historians noted the significance of his victory as a "full circle" of the Philippines from the [People Power Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_Power_Revolution "People Power Revolution"), which deposed [his father](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos "Ferdinand Marcos") from the presidency, thus marking the [Marcos family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcos_family "Marcos family")'s return to national power after 36 years.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Associated_Press-147)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-148)[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-WaPo-149) Marcos's presidential campaign received criticism from fact-checkers and disinformation scholars, who found his campaign to be driven by historical negationism aimed at [rehabilitating the Marcos brand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_distortion_regarding_Ferdinand_Marcos "Historical distortion regarding Ferdinand Marcos") and smearing his rivals.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-filipinosFallFakeHistory-17) His campaign has also been accused of [whitewashing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitewashing_\(censorship\) "Whitewashing \(censorship\)") the human rights abuses and [plunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unexplained_wealth_of_the_Marcos_family "Unexplained wealth of the Marcos family"), estimated at 5 to 13 billion dollars, that took place during his father's presidency.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-filipinosFallFakeHistory-17) _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")_ has noted how the historical distortionism of the Marcoses has been underway since the 2000s, while _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_ cited his convictions of tax fraud, including his refusal to pay his family's estate taxes, and misrepresentation of his education at the [University of Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford "University of Oxford").[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-150)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-151)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-152)[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-153)
His majority was the largest since [1981](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_Philippine_presidential_election_and_referendum "1981 Philippine presidential election and referendum") (surpassing his father's 18,309,360 votes); as the opposition boycotted that election, it is the largest majority since [1969](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_Philippine_presidential_election "1969 Philippine presidential election") for a competitive election, and his 31-percentage point margin over his nearest opponent was the greatest since [Ramon Magsaysay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramon_Magsaysay "Ramon Magsaysay") scored a 38-point margin over incumbent President [Elpidio Quirino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elpidio_Quirino "Elpidio Quirino") in [1953](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1953_Philippine_presidential_election "1953 Philippine presidential election"). His vote count was not only the largest ever recorded in a presidential election, but close to the sum total of the two previous records combined.
On June 20, 2022, Marcos announced that he will serve as the [Secretary of Agriculture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_Agriculture_\(Philippines\) "Secretary of Agriculture \(Philippines\)") in concurrent capacity.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-154)
In the 2022 elections, according to their statements of campaign contributions, Bongbong Marcos and Sara Duterte received tens of millions of pesos in campaign contributions from contractors, despite an election ban on taking donations from firms that do business with the Philippine government.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-:02-155)
