### Early actions
On June 30, 2022, at 12:00 noon [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Standard_Time "Philippine Standard Time"), Marcos Jr. took the oath of office as the 17th [President of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Philippines "President of the Philippines") at the [National Museum of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum_of_the_Philippines "National Museum of the Philippines") and was administered the oath by Chief Justice [Alexander Gesmundo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Gesmundo "Alexander Gesmundo").[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-156)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_officially_declared_Philippines'_next_president-157) At concurrent capacity, Marcos appointed himself as [Secretary of Agriculture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_Agriculture_\(Philippines\) "Secretary of Agriculture \(Philippines\)"), in order to address inflation and personally monitor the food and agricultural sectors, while enacting efforts to boost farm outputs through various loan programs, affordable pricing measures, and machinery assistance.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_Names_Himself_Agriculture_Chief_to_Tackle_Food_Cost-158) Marcos's first [executive order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_executive_orders_by_Bongbong_Marcos "List of executive orders by Bongbong Marcos") as president were abolishing two offices: the [Presidential Anti Corruption Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Anti-Corruption_Commission "Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission") and the Office of the [Cabinet Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_Secretary_\(Philippines\) "Cabinet Secretary \(Philippines\)").[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-159)
The next day after his inauguration, Marcos signed a memorandum seeking to provide free train rides to students, and extends the free rides of the [EDSA Carousel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EDSA_Carousel "EDSA Carousel") until the end of December 2022.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-DOTr:_Marcos_extends_free_EDSA_Carousel_bus_rides,_OKs_free_train_rides_for_students-160) Twelve days later, on July 13, 2022, Marcos announced that the free train rides will only be limited to students using the [LRT Line 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LRT_Line_2 "LRT Line 2"), due to the line's access points to the [University Belt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_Belt "University Belt").[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-DOTr:_Free_train_rides_for_students_now_only_on_LRT2-161)
Two days after his inauguration, on July 2, 2022, Marcos [vetoed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vetoed "Vetoed") a bill sponsored by his sister Senator [Imee Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imee_Marcos "Imee Marcos") that aimed to create a [free economic zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_economic_zone "Free economic zone") within [New Manila International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Manila_International_Airport "New Manila International Airport"). Bongbong Marcos said that the bill would cite "substantial fiscal risks", lacked coherences with existing laws, and the proposed economic zone's location near the existing [Clark Freeport and Special Economic Zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clark_Freeport_and_Special_Economic_Zone "Clark Freeport and Special Economic Zone"); Marcos also called for further studies in establishing the planned economic zone.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bongbong_Marcos_vetoes_bill_on_Bulacan_Airport_City_ecozone-162) On the same day, Marcos also ordered that the list of [Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pantawid_Pamilyang_Pilipino_Program "Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program") beneficiaries to be cleansed after receiving reports of unqualified beneficiaries receiving cash assistance grants and downturned calls to surrender their accounts.
On July 5, 2022, five days after his inauguration, Marcos held his first cabinet meeting, which was delayed during his inauguration, and laid out his first agenda, which primarily focuses on reviving the economy in the midst of the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_Philippines "COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines"). During the meeting, Marcos led the discussions with his economic managers, [Finance Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_Finance_\(Philippines\) "Secretary of Finance \(Philippines\)") [Benjamin Diokno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Diokno "Benjamin Diokno"), [National Economic and Development Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Economic_and_Development_Authority "National Economic and Development Authority") Secretary [Arsenio Balisacan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenio_Balisacan "Arsenio Balisacan"), and [Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangko_Sentral_ng_Pilipinas "Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas") Governor [Felipe Medalla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felipe_Medalla "Felipe Medalla"), to give a briefing about the country's economic status, and to lay out plans to further revive the country's economy, while combating inflation.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-President_Marcos_focuses_on_PH_economy_in_first_Cabinet_meeting-163)[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bongbong_Marcos_holds_first_Cabinet_meeting-164)[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_holds_first_Cabinet_meeting;_focus_on_PH_economy-165) Marcos also tackled issues regarding food security, transportation issues, and the reopening of face-to-face classes within the year.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-President_Marcos_focuses_on_PH_economy_in_first_Cabinet_meeting-163) On July 23, 2022, Marcos has vetoed a bill which seeks to strengthen the Office of the Government Corporate Counsel (OGCC), as he cited that several provisions of the bill are "inequitable".[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bongbong_Marcos_vetoes_bill_strengthening_OGCC-166)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-BBM_vetoes_bill_for_govt_lawyers-167)
On July 25, 2022, the same day of his first [State of the Nation Address](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_State_of_the_Nation_Address_\(Philippines\) "2022 State of the Nation Address \(Philippines\)"), Marcos allowed Republic Act No. 11900, known as the [Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products Regulation Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaporized_Nicotine_and_Non-Nicotine_Products_Regulation_Act "Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products Regulation Act") to lapse into law. The law became controversial, due to the hounding health risks regarding the usage of [electronic cigarettes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_cigarette "Electronic cigarette") and [heated tobacco products](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heated_tobacco_product "Heated tobacco product").[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Controversial_bill_lowering_the_age_for_vape_access_lapses_into_law:_Palace-168) In an effort to boost the country's booster shot campaign, Marcos launched the "PinasLakas" campaign to continue administering [COVID-19 booster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_booster "COVID-19 booster") doses within the public, by targeting a total of at least 39 million Filipinos to get their booster shots.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-PinasLakas_administers_3.4M_1st_booster_dose_in_100_days-169)
Two days after his first State of the Nation Address, following a meeting with Solicitor General [Menardo Guevarra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menardo_Guevarra "Menardo Guevarra"), Presidential Legal Adviser [Juan Ponce Enrile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Ponce_Enrile "Juan Ponce Enrile"), Executive Secretary [Vic Rodriguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vic_Rodriguez_\(lawyer\) "Vic Rodriguez \(lawyer\)"), Foreign Affairs Secretary [Enrique Manalo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enrique_Manalo "Enrique Manalo"), Justice Secretary [Jesus Crispin Remulla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_Crispin_Remulla "Jesus Crispin Remulla"), and former presidential spokesman and lawyer [Harry Roque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Roque "Harry Roque") on July 27, 2022, Marcos expressed that the Philippines has no intention of rejoining the [International Criminal Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court "International Criminal Court"), as the death cases linked to the country's [drug war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_drug_war "Philippine drug war") of [his predecessor's administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Rodrigo_Duterte "Presidency of Rodrigo Duterte") are already being investigated by the government, and stated that the government is taking the necessary steps regarding the deaths.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-PH_has_no_intention_of_rejoining_ICC:_Marcos-170)
On July 30, 2022, Marcos vetoed a bill which grants tax exemption on poll workers' [honoraria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honoraria "Honoraria") and the creation of a transport safety board, stating that the honoraria "counters the objective of the government's [Comprehensive Tax Reform Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_Reform_for_Acceleration_and_Inclusion_Law "Tax Reform for Acceleration and Inclusion Law")", while mentioning that the proposed creation of a transport safety board "undertakes the functions by the different agencies" within the [transport sector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transportation_in_the_Philippines "Transportation in the Philippines").[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bongbong_Marcos_vetoes_transport_safety_board,_tax-free_poll_workers%E2%80%99_honoraria_bills-171)[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_explains_veto_on_bill_making_tax-exempt_teachers%E2%80%99_poll_service_pay-172)
### Domestic policy
#### Agriculture and agrarian reforms
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/PBBM_holds_a_tour_and_inspection_of_another_Kadiwa_ng_Pangulo_%28KNP%29_outlet_in_Koronadal_City%2C_South_Cotabato_%2803%29.jpg/250px-PBBM_holds_a_tour_and_inspection_of_another_Kadiwa_ng_Pangulo_%28KNP%29_outlet_in_Koronadal_City%2C_South_Cotabato_%2803%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PBBM_holds_a_tour_and_inspection_of_another_Kadiwa_ng_Pangulo_\(KNP\)_outlet_in_Koronadal_City,_South_Cotabato_\(03\).jpg)Marcos at a Kadiwa Project outlet in [Koronadal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koronadal "Koronadal"), [South Cotabato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Cotabato "South Cotabato"), in June 2023
Subsequently serving as the Secretary of Agriculture, Marcos launched initiatives which aims to improve domestic agricultural output and production, while expanding measures to further establish a farm-to-market approach in providing agricultural products to local markets and far flung areas.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_wants_to_accelerate_efforts_to_build_agricultural_sector_back-173)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bongbong_Marcos_orders_DA:_Create_farm-to-market_road_masterplan-174) In August 2022, as [high sugar prices impacted the country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Philippine_sugar_crisis "2022 Philippine sugar crisis") due to the effects of [Typhoon Odette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoon_Odette "Typhoon Odette") in December 2021, the [Sugar Regulatory Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar_Regulatory_Administration "Sugar Regulatory Administration") (SRA) in August 2022 released an order to import 300,000 metric tons (660,000,000 lb) of sugar, which is aimed to reduce costs and increase the sugar stockpiles. A few days later, Marcos rejected the proposed importation,[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-175) and Malacañang deemed the move as illegal, as the move was made without Marcos's approval, nor signed by him.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-MB-ProbeSugar-176) SRA Undersecretary Leocadio Sebastian later apologized for the move and later resigned his post on Marcos; behalf,[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-177) prompting SRA Administrator Hermenegildo Serafica and SRA board member Roland Beltran to follow suit a few days later.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-178) The move also caused Malacañang to instigate reforms within the SRA organization,[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-179) and launched a campaign into alleged efforts of using the sugar order as a "cover measure" for [hoarding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoarding "Hoarding") by sugar traders.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_urged_to_crack_down_on_sugar_hoarders-180)
In November 2022, Marcos expanded the Kadiwa Project launched by the Duterte administration, which aims to offer fresh local produces to local markets and other key areas in lower prices, and creates a direct farm-to-market approach of goods and services.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Kadiwa_store_program_eyed_until_February,_March_%E2%80%94_Bongbong_Marcos-181)[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Expanded_Kadiwa_store_project_good_for_farmers,_consumers,_agri_group_says-182) The programs is located in various areas throughout the country and temporarily occupies various facilities owned by local governments. The move is also aimed to be expanded permanently to accommodate more consumers affected by inflation.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_eyes_permanent_Kadiwa_stores_nationwide-183)
In January 2023, amid [rising prices of onions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%932023_Philippine_onion_crisis "2022–2023 Philippine onion crisis") in the country, Marcos approved the importation of 21,060 metric tons (46,430,000 lb) of onions to cater the gap caused by low local outputs,[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Onion_woes_'a_demand_and_supply_situation'_Marcos_says_as_prices_remain_high-184) and stated that the government was "left without a choice" despite approving the smuggled onions to be supplied in local markets.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_says_government_had_no_choice_but_import_onions_to_meet_demand-185)
Marcos signed his fourth executive order on September 14, 2022, which establishes a one-year [moratorium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moratorium_\(law\) "Moratorium \(law\)") on the [amortization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amortization_\(accounting\) "Amortization \(accounting\)") and [interest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interest_\(economics\) "Interest \(economics\)") payments of [agrarian reform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agrarian_reform "Agrarian reform") beneficiaries. The move is seen to assist farmers from debt payments and allows a flexible approach in financial assistance.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-186)
In July 2023, Marcos signed the [New Agrarian Emancipation Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Agrarian_Emancipation_Act "New Agrarian Emancipation Act"), freeing at least 600,000 agrarian reform beneficiaries of decades-old debts worth ₱57-billion under the [Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comprehensive_Agrarian_Reform_Program "Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program").[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-187)
After serving as Secretary of Agriculture for over a year that was marked by a rise in food prices, Marcos relinquished his position and appointed [Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Tiu_Laurel_Jr. "Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr."), president of a deep-sea fishing company and a donor to Marcos's 2022 presidential election campaign.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-188)
#### Defense
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/2025-07-22_%E2%80%93_PBBM_receives_high_praise_from_U.S._President_Donald_J._Trump_%2801%29.jpg/250px-2025-07-22_%E2%80%93_PBBM_receives_high_praise_from_U.S._President_Donald_J._Trump_%2801%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2025-07-22_%E2%80%93_PBBM_receives_high_praise_from_U.S._President_Donald_J._Trump_\(01\).jpg)Marcos with United States president [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") at the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House"), [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), in July 2025 [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/2026-05-28_%E2%80%93_President_Marcos_thanks_Japan_for_swift_aid_during_Navotas_landfill_fire_%2801%29.jpg/250px-2026-05-28_%E2%80%93_President_Marcos_thanks_Japan_for_swift_aid_during_Navotas_landfill_fire_%2801%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2026-05-28_%E2%80%93_President_Marcos_thanks_Japan_for_swift_aid_during_Navotas_landfill_fire_\(01\).jpg)Marcos with Japanese prime minister [Sanae Takaichi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanae_Takaichi "Sanae Takaichi") at the [Naikaku Sōri Daijin Kantei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naikaku_S%C5%8Dri_Daijin_Kantei "Naikaku Sōri Daijin Kantei"), [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo"), in May 2026
In August 2022, the Marcos administration said it was considering ordering helicopters from the [United States military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_military "United States military"), such as the [Boeing CH-47 Chinook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_CH-47_Chinook "Boeing CH-47 Chinook"), to replace the 16 Russian [Mil Mi-17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mil_Mi-17 "Mil Mi-17") military helicopters purchased by the Duterte administration, but cancelled the program a few days before the end of Duterte's term out of concerns about existing [United States sanctions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_sanctions "United States sanctions") such as the [Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Countering_America's_Adversaries_Through_Sanctions_Act "Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act") (CAATSA) and possible future sanctions in response to the ongoing [2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine"). Negotiations are also ongoing to procure limited units which was paid by the government to [Rosoboronexport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosoboronexport "Rosoboronexport").[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_Turns_to_US_To_Fill_Canceled_Russian_Helicopter_Contract-189)[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_committed_to_continuing_AFP_modernization_program_%E2%80%93_military_official-190)
Marcos expressed support for the [AFP Modernization Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFP_Modernization_Act "AFP Modernization Act"),[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bongbong_Marcos_eyes_%E2%80%98stronger,_bigger%E2%80%99_air_force_to_defend_PH-191) which aims to boost the country's defense capabilities. Stating that the country's external security situation is becoming "more complex and unpredictable", Marcos ordered the [Armed Forces of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_Forces_of_the_Philippines "Armed Forces of the Philippines") to shift its focus on its defense operations against external threats, due to the lower risks in the country's insurgencies, the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine"), and the potential Chinese invasion of Taiwan.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-PBBM_assures_support_for_AFP_modernization,_enhanced_troop_readiness-192)[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bongbong_Marcos:_AFP_modernization_to_continue_%E2%80%98to_address_present_dangers%E2%80%99_PH_is_facing-193)
During the 125th-anniversary celebration of the [Philippine Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Navy "Philippine Navy"), Marcos announced plans to acquire the Philippines' first [submarine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submarine "Submarine"). The French-based [Naval Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Group "Naval Group"), along with other contenders, has offered its [Scorpène-class submarines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scorp%C3%A8ne-class_submarine "Scorpène-class submarine") to strengthen the Navy.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-194)
With an aim to enhance the country's defense capabilities, Marcos has approved the "Re-Horizon 3" of the AFP Modernization Program, which is also known as the RAFMP. The $35 billion plan revised modernization program will be spread out over 10 years and aims to modernize the [Armed Forces of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_Forces_of_the_Philippines "Armed Forces of the Philippines") based on the Comprehensive Archipelagic Defense Concept (CADC), a defense concept aimed at strengthening the country's external defense deterrence by projecting power within the [Philippine's 200 nautical mile exclusive economic zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exclusive_economic_zone_of_the_Philippines "Exclusive economic zone of the Philippines"), [Benham Rise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benham_Rise "Benham Rise"), the [Luzon Strait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luzon_Strait "Luzon Strait"), and the [Sulu Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulu_Sea "Sulu Sea") through inter-island defenses doctrines, multi-layered domain strategies, and long-range strike capabilities.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-CADC_to_allow_PH_to_defend_sea_lanes_of_communication-195) The concept also aims to strengthen the country's aerial and maritime domain awareness, connectivity, and intelligence capabilities.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_approved_AFP_modernization's_'Horizon_3'_%E2%80%94Teodoro-196)[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-AFP_modernization's_Horizon_3_to_focus_on_archipelagic_defense-197)[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_Jr._approves_military_procurement_%E2%80%98wish_list%E2%80%99-198)
On April 15, 2025, Marcos signed into law Republic Act No. 12174, prohibiting the development, production, stockpiling, and use of [chemical weapons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_weapons "Chemical weapons") in the Philippines.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-199)
#### Education
In August 2022, despite the low [COVID-19 vaccination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_vaccination_in_the_Philippines "COVID-19 vaccination in the Philippines") rate among Filipino students with a total vaccination rate of only 19%, Marcos, along with [Vice President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_Philippines "Vice President of the Philippines") and [Education Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_Education_\(Philippines\) "Secretary of Education \(Philippines\)") [Sara Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Duterte "Sara Duterte"), reopened onsite classes throughout the country, with 46% or 24,000 schools throughout the country reopening their classes on August 22. Meanwhile, 29,721 schools were allowed to continue implementing [blended learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blended_learning "Blended learning") from August to October 2022,[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-200) while the full implementation of onsite classes began within November 2022, with 97.5% of public schools returning to onsite classes, while the remaining 2.36% of classes were temporarily held online due to the effects of [Severe Tropical Storm Paeng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_Storm_Nalgae "Tropical Storm Nalgae").[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-DepEd:_97.5%_ng_public_schools,_nakabalik_na_sa_full_F2F_classes-201)
Marcos also reviewed the implementation of the [K–12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%E2%80%9312 "K–12") program as part of his push to modernize the [country's education system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education_in_the_Philippines "Education in the Philippines"), and laid out measures such as system reforms to address the lack of jobs and potential job mismatches, reviewing the usage of English as a medium of instruction in schools, and improving the country's education technology systems.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos:_K-12_program_under_careful_review-202)[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_wants_review_of_education_curriculum_to_address_jobs_mismatch-203) Marcos also expressed his support to modernize the country's schools by improving science-related subjects and courses, theoretical aptitude, and vocational skills.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_vows_upgrade_of_schools,_teachers-204)[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bongbong_Marcos_vows_reform_in_PH_education:_Not_in_history_but_in_sciences,_vocational_skills-205)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/PBBM_approves_NEDA%E2%80%99s_PH_Development_Plan_for_2023-2028.jpg/250px-PBBM_approves_NEDA%E2%80%99s_PH_Development_Plan_for_2023-2028.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PBBM_approves_NEDA%E2%80%99s_PH_Development_Plan_for_2023-2028.jpg)Marcos convenes a [NEDA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Economic_and_Development_Authority "National Economic and Development Authority") meeting at Malacañang Palace in December 2022, approving the Philippine Development Plan for 2023–2028.
The Marcos administration approved the inclusion of the Philippines to the [Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_Comprehensive_Economic_Partnership "Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership") (RCEP) [free trade agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_trade_agreement "Free trade agreement"), which was ratified by the Senate on February 21, 2023.[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-216) His administration also formed the [Private Sector Advisory Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_Sector_Advisory_Council "Private Sector Advisory Council"), a council that will advise the President on economic affairs.[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-217)[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-218)
Marcos issued an executive order suspending _e-sabong_ (online cockfighting) operations in the country.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-219) He also issued an executive order banning [Philippine offshore gaming operators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_offshore_gaming_operator "Philippine offshore gaming operator") (POGOs), citing concerns for national security.[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-220)[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-221) Residential condominiums and offices markets were severely affected following the POGO ban, which saw a vacancy rate of up to 20.5% following the surrender of spaces and non-renewals of leases from POGOs.[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-222)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/PBBM-World_Economic_Forum-PH4.jpg/250px-PBBM-World_Economic_Forum-PH4.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PBBM-World_Economic_Forum-PH4.jpg)Marcos with [European Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Commission "European Commission") president [Ursula von der Leyen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ursula_von_der_Leyen "Ursula von der Leyen") and Swiss president [Alain Berset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Berset "Alain Berset") at the [World Economic Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Economic_Forum "World Economic Forum") in [Davos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davos "Davos"), Switzerland, in January 2023
In the early years of his presidency, he sought to prioritize the country's post-[COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_Philippines "COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines") economy as highlighted by his economic agenda,[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bongbong_Marcos_team_presents_8-point_economic_agenda-223) lifting the lockdowns and facemask restrictions. His administration sought to target a 6.5 to 7.5% [real gross domestic product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_gross_domestic_product "Real gross domestic product") (GDP) growth rate, with a 6.5 to 8% annual real GDP growth rate, a 9% or single-digit [poverty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_in_the_Philippines "Poverty in the Philippines") rate by 2028, a 3% national [government deficit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_deficit "Government deficit")-to-GDP ratio by 2028, lowering the country's [debt-to-GDP ratio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debt-to-GDP_ratio "Debt-to-GDP ratio") to less than 60% by 2025, and securing an [upper middle-income status](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developing_country "Developing country") by 2024 with a [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")4,256 income per capita, which is part of his 2023–2028 fiscal strategy. Marcos also supports the creation of additional [economic zones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_economic_zone "Special economic zone") in various areas of the country to attract investments and laid out plans to impose [digital taxes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_tax "Digital tax") and improve the country's tax compliance procedures which should improve revenue collections and cut the country's debts, while maintaining the country's disbursements at above 20 percent of its GDP.[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-What_Marcos_said_in_his_first_SONA,_from_A-Z-224)[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_bares_plans_for_economic_recovery_in_first_SONA-225)
#### Insurgency
This section is an excerpt from [Presidency of Bongbong Marcos § Insurgency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Bongbong_Marcos#Insurgency "Presidency of Bongbong Marcos").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Presidency_of_Bongbong_Marcos&action=edit)]
To harmonize the Bangsamoro peace agreements of the [1976 Tripoli Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Tripoli_Agreement "1976 Tripoli Agreement"), the [1996 Final Peace Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Final_Peace_Agreement "1996 Final Peace Agreement") and the [2014 Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comprehensive_Agreement_on_the_Bangsamoro "Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro"), the [Office of the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_the_Presidential_Adviser_on_Peace,_Reconciliation_and_Unity "Office of the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity") facilitated the participation of the [Moro National Liberation Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moro_National_Liberation_Front "Moro National Liberation Front") (MNLF) in the [Bangsamoro Transition Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangsamoro_Transition_Authority "Bangsamoro Transition Authority") (BTA). On August 14, 2022, Marcos appointed new members of the BTA, and included Abdulkarim Misuari and Nurrheda Misuari, son and daughter of [Moro National Liberation Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moro_National_Liberation_Front "Moro National Liberation Front") leader [Nur Misuari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nur_Misuari "Nur Misuari"), in an effort to unite former warring members of the MNLF and the [Moro Islamic Liberation Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moro_Islamic_Liberation_Front "Moro Islamic Liberation Front") under one Bangsamoro autonomous government.[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-226)[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-227)
#### Communist policy
Amid the weakening of the communist fronts by the military, in May 2023, Marcos directed the "recalibration" of the [NTF-ELCAC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NTF-ELCAC "NTF-ELCAC"), an anti-insurgency task force, to shift its previous "aggressive" policy and become "bringers of peace".[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-228) Marcos appointed Vice President [Sara Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Duterte "Sara Duterte") as co-vice chair of the NTF-ELCAC.[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-229) As part of his administration's peace initiatives, in November 2023, Marcos granted amnesty to former rebels of the [Communist Party of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_the_Philippines "Communist Party of the Philippines")-[New People's Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_People's_Army "New People's Army")-[National Democratic Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democratic_Front_\(Philippines\) "National Democratic Front \(Philippines\)") (CPP-NPA-NDF), [Moro Islamic Liberation Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moro_Islamic_Liberation_Front "Moro Islamic Liberation Front") (MILF), and [Moro National Liberation Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moro_National_Liberation_Front "Moro National Liberation Front") (MNLF); he also granted amnesty to members of the Rebolusyonaryong Partido ng Manggagawa ng Pilipinas/Revolutionary Proletarian Army/Alex Boncayao Brigade (RPMP-RPA-ABB).[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-230)
In a reversal of Duterte's policy, the Marcos administration and the NDF issued a joint statement on November 28, 2023, announcing the revival of peace talks between the two parties,[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-231)[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Presidency_of_Bongbong_Marcos_DiplomatStrangio-232) with the government side to be led by retired general [Emmanuel Bautista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Bautista "Emmanuel Bautista") and Special Presidential Assistant [Antonio Lagdameo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Lagdameo "Antonio Lagdameo") and the NDF side to be led by [Luis Jalandoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Jalandoni "Luis Jalandoni").[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-233)[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Presidency_of_Bongbong_Marcos_DiplomatStrangio-232) Vice President Duterte asked Marcos to reconsider the plan to hold peace talks which she called an "agreement with the devil", while Speaker [Martin Romualdez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Romualdez "Martin Romualdez") deemed the decision to be a "moral imperative" for the country.[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-234) Negotiations between the Marcos administration and the NDF began in [Oslo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo "Oslo") as early as 2022, but were withheld from the public.[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-235)
After the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_Philippines "Supreme Court of the Philippines") ruled in May 2024 that [red-tagging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red-tagging_in_the_Philippines "Red-tagging in the Philippines") threatens a person's right to life, liberty, or security, [Human Rights Watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Rights_Watch "Human Rights Watch") and [Karapatan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karapatan "Karapatan") called on Marcos to abolish the NTF-ELCAC. Marcos rejected the calls for abolition, saying the task force was instrumental in reducing the country's internal security threat.[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-236)[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-237) In July 2024, Duterte resigned as co-vice chairperson of NTF-ELCAC.[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-238)

In 2022, the Marcos administration launched the BroadBand ng Masa Program (BBMP) to provide free WiFi connections in remote areas.[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-239) To "boost government initiatives against scams committed through text and online messages", Marcos signed [his first law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIM_Registration_Act "SIM Registration Act"), which mandated [SIM card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIM_card "SIM card") registration;[[238]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-240) by the end of the July 2023 deadline, a total of 113.9 million SIM cards were registered, and about 54 million unregistered mobile numbers were deactivated.[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-241)
### Foreign policy
See also: [List of international presidential trips made by Bongbong Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_presidential_trips_made_by_Bongbong_Marcos "List of international presidential trips made by Bongbong Marcos")
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Bongbong_Marcos_delivered_remarks_at_the_General_Assembly_Hall_for_2022_UNGA.jpg/250px-Bongbong_Marcos_delivered_remarks_at_the_General_Assembly_Hall_for_2022_UNGA.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bongbong_Marcos_delivered_remarks_at_the_General_Assembly_Hall_for_2022_UNGA.jpg)Marcos addresses the [77th session of the United Nations General Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventy-seventh_session_of_the_United_Nations_General_Assembly "Seventy-seventh session of the United Nations General Assembly") on September 20, 2022. [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fe/Bongbong_Marcos_and_Volodymyr_Zelenskyy.jpg/250px-Bongbong_Marcos_and_Volodymyr_Zelenskyy.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bongbong_Marcos_and_Volodymyr_Zelenskyy.jpg)Marcos speaks with Ukrainian president [Volodymyr Zelenskyy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy "Volodymyr Zelenskyy") during [the latter's visit to Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_presidential_trips_made_by_Volodymyr_Zelenskyy "List of international presidential trips made by Volodymyr Zelenskyy") on June 3, 2024. [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/2026-06-18_%E2%80%93_PBBM_highlights_huge_potential_of_Philippine-Russia_trade%2C_economic_cooperation_%2801%29.jpg/250px-2026-06-18_%E2%80%93_PBBM_highlights_huge_potential_of_Philippine-Russia_trade%2C_economic_cooperation_%2801%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2026-06-18_%E2%80%93_PBBM_highlights_huge_potential_of_Philippine-Russia_trade,_economic_cooperation_\(01\).jpg)Marcos meets with Russian president [Vladimir Putin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin "Vladimir Putin") during a visit to [Kazan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazan "Kazan") on June 18, 2026.
Early in his presidency, Marcos promised to continue his predecessor [Rodrigo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte "Rodrigo Duterte")'s foreign policy of being "friends to all, enemies to none".[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-242) Marcos initially sought [closer ties with China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China%E2%80%93Philippines_relations "China–Philippines relations"),[[241]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-243) but has since been increasingly seen as more pro-American than Duterte in an attempt to create a centrist-style balancing act between the two superpowers.[[242]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos:_PH_rejects_claims_SCS_disputes_due_to_rivalry_of_2_'powerful_countries'-244)[[243]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-The_Philippines%E2%80%99_Quest_for_Balance:_Marcos%E2%80%99_Foreign_Policy-245)[[244]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-The_Philippines_Is_America%E2%80%99s_New_Star_Ally_in_Asia-246)[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_Jr_fashions_a_flexible_foreign_policy_for_the_Philippines-247)[[246]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-248) During his first [State of the Nation Address](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_State_of_the_Nation_Address_\(Philippines\) "2022 State of the Nation Address \(Philippines\)"), Marcos promised to "not preside over any process that will abandon even one-square inch of territory of the Republic of the Philippines to any foreign power".[[247]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bongbong_Marcos_stands_firm_on_protecting_PH_waters-249)
Under his presidency, Marcos intensified the Philippines' cooperation on both economic and defense arrangements to [Western countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_countries "Western countries"), such as the United States, Japan, Australia, and the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union"), while strengthening its defense posture within the region.[[248]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Sea_Change:_%E2%80%98Bongbong%E2%80%99_Marcos_and_the_Future_of_the_South_China_Sea-250)[[249]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Philippine_President_Marcos_Jr.%E2%80%99s_Foreign_Policy_Emphasizes_Cooperation-251) Marcos approved the designation of four additional bases to be used by the United States military under the [Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced_Defense_Cooperation_Agreement "Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement").[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-252) In May 2024, the Philippines and the United States held its largest [Balikatan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balikatan "Balikatan") military exercises, fueling concerns from local civilians who fear they would be affected in any future war between the US and China.[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-253) The deployment of the United States' Typhon Weapons System in an undisclosed location in northern [Luzon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luzon "Luzon") also caught the attention of Russian president [Vladimir Putin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin "Vladimir Putin"), who said that Russia should resume producing nuclear-capable missiles and consider where to deploy them.[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-254)
Marcos called on all involved parties on the South China Sea to abide by the 1982 [United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Convention_on_the_Law_of_the_Sea "United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea") in order to diffuse potential conflicts in the future.[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Bongbong_Marcos:_Abide_by_Unclos_to_prevent_conflict_in_South_China_Sea-255) Due to Marcos's "transparency thrust" in dealing with the aggressive actions of the [Chinese Coast Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Coast_Guard "Chinese Coast Guard") and the Chinese [Maritime Militia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maritime_Militia "Maritime Militia"), [China–Philippines relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China%E2%80%93Philippines_relations "China–Philippines relations") have significantly deteriorated during Marcos's tenure, with increasing tensions over [territorial disputes in the South China Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territorial_disputes_in_the_South_China_Sea "Territorial disputes in the South China Sea")[[254]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Philippines_strikes_security_deals_as_tensions_rise_with_China_at_sea-256)[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-257) and the Philippines withdrawing from the [Belt and Road initiative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belt_and_Road_initiative "Belt and Road initiative").[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-258)
### Human rights
This section is an excerpt from [Human rights in the Philippines § Marcos Jr. administration (2022–present)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights_in_the_Philippines#Marcos_Jr._administration_\(2022%E2%80%93present\) "Human rights in the Philippines").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Human_rights_in_the_Philippines&action=edit)]
President Bongbong Marcos promised to uphold human rights during his term.[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Human_rights_in_the_Philippines_:3-259) The Philippines stated in 2022 that it was committed to cooperate with United Nations human rights mechanisms. The United Nations noted the failure of law enforcement to address human rights violations and recommended that the Philippines review all killings in the government's drug war.[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-260)
Drug war killings, attacks on activists, harassment of media, and red-tagging have continued. During the first year of Bongbong Marcos's term, there were 336 drug war killings, mostly during police operations,[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Human_rights_in_the_Philippines_:3-259) and 8 cases of forced disappearances.[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Human_rights_in_the_Philippines_:4-261) In 2024, the Commission on Human Rights said that human rights violations under the Duterte and Bongbong Marcos presidencies were almost similar.[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Human_rights_in_the_Philippines_:10-262) The Defend NGO Alliance stated that the human rights situation may have worsened under Bongbong Marcos. The alliance called for the abolition of repressive agencies and policies, such as the National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict and the Anti-Terrorism Act.[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-263)
As of November 2024, four journalists have been killed while doing their jobs under the Bongbong Marcos presidency. This includes broadcaster [Percy Lapid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_of_Percy_Lapid "Killing of Percy Lapid") who was red-tagged and subsequently killed near his home. Journalists also continue to be red-tagged, harassed, or jailed, such as [Frenchie Mae Cumpio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frenchie_Mae_Cumpio "Frenchie Mae Cumpio"), who is detained on allegations of terror financing.[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Human_rights_in_the_Philippines_:10-262)
Congress representatives and human rights groups have urged the Bongbong Marcos administration to rejoin the Rome Statute and the International Criminal Court.[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-264) As of March 2025, the government has refused to rejoin the International Criminal Court.[[263]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-265)
### Impeachment complaint
On January 19, 2026, an impeachment complaint was filed against Marcos before the [House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Representatives_of_the_Philippines "House of Representatives of the Philippines") on charges related to the arrest of Rodrigo Duterte, his alleged drug use and involvement in the flood control scandal and issues over the national budget. The complaint was filed by lawyer Andre de Jesus and endorsed by [Pusong Pinoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pusong_Pinoy "Pusong Pinoy") partylist representative [Jett Nisay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jett_Nisay?action=edit&redlink=1 "Jett Nisay \(page does not exist\)").[[264]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-266)
## Court cases
### Income and estate tax case convictions
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/af/Protest_vs_Marcos_Tax_Evader.jpg/250px-Protest_vs_Marcos_Tax_Evader.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Protest_vs_Marcos_Tax_Evader.jpg)Protests against Marcos over his involvement in tax evasion in September 2022
On June 27, 1990, a special tax audit team of the [Bureau of Internal Revenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Internal_Revenue_\(Philippines\) "Bureau of Internal Revenue \(Philippines\)") (BIR) investigated the tax liabilities and obligations of the late Ferdinand Marcos, who died on September 29, 1989. The investigation disclosed in a 1991 memorandum that the [Marcos family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcos_family "Marcos family") had failed to file [estate tax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estate_tax "Estate tax") returns and several [income tax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Income_tax "Income tax") returns covering the years of 1982 to 1986 in violation of the National Internal Revenue Code.[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-gr-120880-267)
The BIR also issued a deficiency estate tax assessment against the estate of the late Ferdinand Marcos in 1991 for unpaid estate taxes from 1982 to 1985, and 1985 to 1986, totaling ₱23,293,607,638 (₱97,792,696,739 in 2022). Formal assessment notices were served to Bongbong Marcos at his office at the [Batasang Pambansa Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batasang_Pambansa_Complex "Batasang Pambansa Complex") on October 20, 1992, who was then the representative of the 2nd District of Ilocos Norte. Several notices of [levy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax "Tax") were also issued by the BIR February 22, 1993, to May 26, 1993, to satisfy the deficiency of estate tax returns, to no avail.[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-gr-120880-267)
On March 12, 1993, lawyer Loreto Ata, representing Bongbong Marcos, called the attention of the BIR to notify them of any action taken by the BIR against his client. Bongbong Marcos then filed an instant petition on June 25, 1993, for _[certiorari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certiorari "Certiorari")_ and prohibition to contest the estate tax deficiency assessment.[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-gr-120880-267)
On July 27, 1995, [Quezon City Regional Trial Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_Trial_Court "Regional Trial Court") Judge Benedicto Ulep convicted Marcos to seven years in jail and a fine of US$2,812 (₱138,491 in 2025) plus back taxes for [tax evasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_evasion "Tax evasion") in his failure to file an [income tax return](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Income_tax_return "Income tax return") from the period of 1982 to 1985 while sitting as the vice governor of Ilocos Norte (1980–1983) and as governor of Ilocos Norte (1983–1986).[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-268) Marcos subsequently appealed the decision to the [Court of Appeals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_of_Appeals_of_the_Philippines "Court of Appeals of the Philippines") over his conviction. However, in 1994, the Court of Appeals ruled that the estate tax deficiency assessment had become "final and unappealable", allowing it to be enforced.[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-isko-marcos-estate-tax-269)
On October 31, 1997, the Court of Appeals affirmed its earlier decision with Marcos being convicted for the failure of the filing of an income tax return under Section 45 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1977 while being acquitted of tax evasion under the charge of violating Section 50 of the same statute. In spite of the removal of the penalty of imprisonment, Marcos was ordered the payment of [back income taxes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back_taxes "Back taxes") to the [Bureau of Internal Revenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Internal_Revenue_\(Philippines\) "Bureau of Internal Revenue \(Philippines\)") (BIR) with interest and the issuance of corresponding fines of ₱2,000 per count of non-filing of income tax returns from 1982 to 1984 and ₱30,000 for 1985, plus the accrued interest.[[268]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-270) Marcos later filed a petition for [certiorari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certiorari "Certiorari") to the [Supreme Court of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_Philippines "Supreme Court of the Philippines") over the modified conviction imposed by the Court of Appeals but subsequently withdrew his petition on August 8, 2001, thereby declaring the ruling as final and executory.[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-271)
In 2021, the Quezon City Regional Trial Court certified that there were no records on file of Marcos settling the corresponding tax dues and fines.[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-272)[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-273) However, according to Marcos's campaign team, documents issued by the Supreme Court, the BIR, and a receipt issued by the [Land Bank of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_Bank_of_the_Philippines "Land Bank of the Philippines") state that the tax dues were paid,[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-274)[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-275) while elections commissioner [Rowena Guanzon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rowena_Guanzon "Rowena Guanzon") noted that the documents Marcos submitted to the [Commission on Elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_on_Elections_\(Philippines\) "Commission on Elections \(Philippines\)") were not receipts of taxes paid to the BIR but rather receipts from the Land Bank for lease rentals.[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-276)[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-277) Nevertheless, the [Commission on Elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_on_Elections_\(Philippines\) "Commission on Elections \(Philippines\)") ruled against the consolidated disqualification cases against Marcos and stated that "Further, to prove the absence of any ill-intention and bad faith on his part," Marcos submitted a Bureau of Internal Revenue certification and an official receipt from the Landbank, showing his compliance with the CA decision directing him to pay deficiency income taxes amounting to a little over ₱67,000, including fines and surcharges.[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-278)
The estate tax deficiency assessment issued by the BIR has remained uncollected since the Supreme Court ruling on October 12, 1991. Since the ruling of the Supreme Court in 1997 which had junked the petition of Marcos to contest the estate tax deficiency assessment, under the [Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Fidel_Ramos "Presidency of Fidel Ramos"), [Arroyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Gloria_Macapagal_Arroyo "Presidency of Gloria Macapagal Arroyo"), [Aquino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Benigno_Aquino_III "Presidency of Benigno Aquino III"), and [Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Rodrigo_Duterte "Presidency of Rodrigo Duterte") administrations, the BIR has issued renewed written demands on the Marcos family to pay the estate tax liabilities, which has remained unpaid. As a result, the estate tax deficiency assessment, with penalties, is estimated to have ballooned to ₱203,819,066,829 (₱203.819 billion) as of 2021.[[277]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-marocs-estate-tax-debt-279)
The unpaid estate tax return was used as grounds in one petition to cancel Marcos's certificate of candidacy for president in the 2022 elections. On March 1, 2022, presidential candidate and Manila mayor [Isko Moreno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isko_Moreno "Isko Moreno") said that he would implement the Supreme Court ruling ordering the Marcos family to pay their estate tax debts if elected, vowing to use the proceeds as relief aid (_ayuda_) for victims of the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_Philippines "COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines").[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-isko-marcos-estate-tax-269) [Ernest Ramel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernest_Ramel "Ernest Ramel"), the secretary general of Aksyon Demokratiko, the party of Moreno continuously called out BIR about the issue.[[278]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-280)[[279]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-:1-281)
On March 28, 2022, Senator [Koko Pimentel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koko_Pimentel "Koko Pimentel") filed Senate Resolution No. 998, stating an urgent and pressing need for the Senate to look into why the estate tax has remained uncollected for almost 25 years, which the amount has already been ruled to be due and demandable against the heirs of his father.[[280]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-pimentel-senate-resolution-282)
### 2007 Payanig sa Pasig property case motion
Further information: [Payanig sa Pasig land dispute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payanig_sa_Pasig_land_dispute "Payanig sa Pasig land dispute")
On June 19, 2007,[[281]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-hrclaimpayanig-283) Marcos Jr. filed a motion to intervene in, OCLP v. PCGG, Civil Case Number 0093 at the Sandiganbayan, the Philippines' anti-graft court.[[281]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-hrclaimpayanig-283) The case had been filed by Ortigas & Company, Ltd. Partnership (OCLP) against the Presidential Commission on Good Government (PCGG) over the 18-hectare (44-acre) former Payanig sa Pasig property bordering [Ortigas Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ortigas_Avenue "Ortigas Avenue"), [Julia Vargas Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_Vargas_Avenue "Julia Vargas Avenue"), and [Meralco Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meralco_Avenue "Meralco Avenue") in [Ortigas Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ortigas_Center "Ortigas Center"), [Pasig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasig "Pasig"), which had been the site of the 'Payanig sa Pasig' theme park, but is now the location of various businesses, most notably the [Metrowalk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrowalk "Metrowalk") shopping and recreation complex.[[282]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-abscbnpayanigblock-284)
The PCGG considers the property the "crown jewel" among the properties sequestered from the Marcoses' ill-gotten wealth, estimating its minimum value to be about ₱16.5 billion in March 2015.[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-PCGGSellPayanig2015-285) The property had been surrendered to the PCGG in 1986, as part of the settlement deal of Marcos crony [Jose Yao Campos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_Yao_Campos "Jose Yao Campos"), who was holding the property under various companies on Marcos Sr.'s behalf.[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-CamposAssets-286) Ortigas & Company countered that Marcos Sr. had coerced them to sell the property to him in 1968.[[282]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-abscbnpayanigblock-284) Marcos Jr.'s motion claimed that his father had bought the property legally, but the Sandiganbayan dismissed his motion on October 18, 2008, saying it had already dismissed a similar motion filed years earlier by his mother Imelda.[[285]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-sonappealspayanig-287)
### 2011 Hawaii contempt judgement
In 2011, the Hawaii District Court ruled Bongbong Marcos and his mother Imelda Marcos to be in contempt,[[286]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-PDIBongbongImeldaLoseAppeal-288) fining them US$353.6 million (₱17,414,799,999.93 in 2025) fine for not respecting an injunction from a 1992 judgement in a human rights victims case, which commanded them not to dissipate the assets of Ferdinand Marcos's estate.[[287]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Honolulu_Civil_Beat-289)[[288]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-EnforceUSImeldaBongbongRuling-290) The ruling was upheld by the [US Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Court_of_Appeals_for_the_Ninth_Circuit "United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit") on October 24, 2012, and is believed to be "the largest contempt award ever affirmed by an appellate court."[[288]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-EnforceUSImeldaBongbongRuling-290) While the 1992 case was against Ferdinand Marcos, the 2011 judgment was against Imelda and Bongbong personally.[[289]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-PDIMarcosesInContempt-291) The judgement also effectively barred Imelda and Bongbong from entering any US territory.[[286]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-PDIBongbongImeldaLoseAppeal-288) However, on June 9, 2022, [United States Deputy Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Deputy_Secretary_of_State "United States Deputy Secretary of State") [Wendy Sherman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Sherman "Wendy Sherman")[[290]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-292) clarified in a roundtable discussion with local reporters during a state visit, that as a head of state, Marcos enjoys [diplomatic immunity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomatic_immunity "Diplomatic immunity") in all circumstances, stating that he is welcome to visit the United States under his official role.[[291]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-293)
