Marcos has described his political views as "[conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative "Conservative")" and "[Machiavellian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machiavelli "Machiavelli")".[[292]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-294) He has also described the "spirit of [nationalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationalism "Nationalism")" as a force driving progress in the Philippines.[[293]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-295) Before taking office, Marcos has been described in media reports as a [populist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Populist "Populist").[[294]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-296)[[295]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-297) On social issues, he is in favor of legalizing abortion for rape and incest victims[[296]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-298)[[297]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-299) as well as divorce and same-sex unions.[[298]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-300)[[299]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-301) Marcos is also opposed to reinstating the death penalty for convicted heinous criminals[[300]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-302) and lowering the minimum age of criminal responsibility to 12.[[301]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-303) In terms of economic policy, analysts initially speculated that Marcos would pursue liberal policies as opposed to his protectionist rhetoric during the presidential campaign.[[302]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-304)
### Marcos–Duterte feud
See also: [UniTeam § Aftermath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UniTeam#Aftermath "UniTeam")
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/President_Bongbong_Marcos_meets_former_President_Rodrigo_Duterte_in_Malaca%C3%B1ang_on_August_2%2C_2023.jpg/250px-President_Bongbong_Marcos_meets_former_President_Rodrigo_Duterte_in_Malaca%C3%B1ang_on_August_2%2C_2023.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Bongbong_Marcos_meets_former_President_Rodrigo_Duterte_in_Malaca%C3%B1ang_on_August_2,_2023.jpg)Marcos with his predecessor, [Rodrigo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte "Rodrigo Duterte"), at Malacañang in August 2023
Amid the feud of the Marcos and Duterte clans in late April 2023, House Speaker and Marcos's cousin [Martin Romualdez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Romualdez "Martin Romualdez") said the House of Representatives will probe into an agreement former president [Rodrigo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte "Rodrigo Duterte") made during [his presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Rodrigo_Duterte "Presidency of Rodrigo Duterte") with Chinese leader [Xi Jinping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Jinping "Xi Jinping"). Under the agreement, Duterte agreed to maintain the "status quo" in the South China Sea to avoid escalating a war. Political analyst Ronald Llamas said the probe was engineered by Marcos as a "political payback" to Duterte's verbal attacks and to reduce Duterte's political influence ahead of the 2025 midterm elections.[[303]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-305) The [2025 Philippine general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Philippine_general_election "2025 Philippine general election") saw mixed to unfavorable results for Marcos.
In 2024, Duterte criticized the Marcos administration's curtailment of the [freedom of speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_of_speech "Freedom of speech") in violation of the 1987 [Bill of Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_the_Philippines "Constitution of the Philippines"). Duterte's nationwide "_Hakbang ng Maisug_ " (brave) [prayer rallies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prayer_protest "Prayer protest"), which Duterte said the Marcos administration deliberately aimed to thwart, suffered setbacks and cancellations.[[304]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-HnM-306)[[305]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-307) Duterte, however, said he prayed for Marcos to survive until the end of his term since Duterte does not want himself or his daughter Sara to become president.[[304]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-HnM-306)
In June 2024, Vice President Sara Duterte resigned from the Marcos cabinet and grew critical of Marcos.[[306]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-:0-308) Her first public criticism of Marcos was during the 39th anniversary celebration of [Kingdom of Jesus Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Jesus_Christ "Kingdom of Jesus Christ") within [Davao City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davao_City "Davao City") in late August 2024 during the [police search for Apollo Quiboloy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrest_of_Apollo_Quiboloy "Arrest of Apollo Quiboloy"), where she admitted her regret in supporting Marcos' candidacy as president.[[307]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-309) In November 2024, Philippine authorities [subpoenaed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subpoena "Subpoena") Vice President Duterte after she threatened to have Marcos, his wife Liza, and House Speaker Romualdez assassinated if she were killed. Without naming Duterte, Marcos condemned any sort of "criminal plans" and increased his security, while National Security Adviser [Eduardo Año](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eduardo_A%C3%B1o "Eduardo Año") called the threats a national security concern.[[308]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-310)[[309]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-311) She was ordered to appear before the [National Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Bureau_of_Investigation_\(Philippines\) "National Bureau of Investigation \(Philippines\)"), with such statements potentially leading to criminal charges.[[306]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-:0-308) Marcos, however, expressed openness to the possibility of reconciling with Duterte.[[310]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-312) Despite growing calls for Sara Duterte's impeachment,[[311]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-313)[[312]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-314)[[313]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-315)[[314]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-316) Marcos has repeatedly voiced his opinion against impeaching her, calling it "a storm in a teacup" and considering the move inconsequential to the lives of Filipinos.[[315]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-317)[[316]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-318)[[317]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-319)
On March 11, 2025, [Rodrigo Duterte was detained](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrest_of_Rodrigo_Duterte "Arrest of Rodrigo Duterte") in Manila, following an [arrest warrant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court_investigation_in_the_Philippines "International Criminal Court investigation in the Philippines") from the [International Criminal Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court "International Criminal Court") stemming from an investigation of human rights abuses during Duterte's anti-drug campaign.[[318]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-320)
## Public profile
See also: [Opinion polling on the Bongbong Marcos presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opinion_polling_on_the_Bongbong_Marcos_presidency "Opinion polling on the Bongbong Marcos presidency")
In 2024, _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_\(magazine\) "Time \(magazine\)")_ magazine listed him as one of [the world's 100 most influential people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100").[[319]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-321)[[320]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-322)
### Historical distortionism
Main article: [Historical distortion regarding Ferdinand Marcos § Historical denialism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_distortion_regarding_Ferdinand_Marcos#Historical_denialism "Historical distortion regarding Ferdinand Marcos")
As with other Marcos family members who have stayed in the public eye since their return to the Philippines,[[321]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-CMFR20160310-323)[[322]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-MerlinaHernandoMalipot20180907-324)[[323]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-NikDeYnchausti20160923-325) Marcos has received significant criticism for instances of [historical denialism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_denialism "Historical denialism"), and his trivialization of the human rights violations and economic plunder that took place during the Marcos administration, and of the role he played in the administration.[[324]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-amnestyInternational1975-326)[[325]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-singaporeSwissFunds-327)[[326]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-rapplerNoApologies-328) Specific criticisms have been leveled at Marcos for being unapologetic for human rights violations[[324]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-amnestyInternational1975-326) and ill-gotten wealth[[325]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-singaporeSwissFunds-327) during [his father](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos "Ferdinand Marcos")'s administration.[[327]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-unfazed-329)[[328]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-noDownsides-330)[[329]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-gmaBongToCritics-331)[[326]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-rapplerNoApologies-328) Of the human rights victims, Marcos Jr. said of them in 1999: "They don't want an apology, they want money."[[330]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-onlyWantMoney-332) He then proceeded to state that his family would apologize only if they had done something wrong.
When victims of [human rights abuses during his father's administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#Human_rights_abuses "Ferdinand Marcos") commemorated the 40th year of the proclamation of martial law in 2012, Marcos Jr. dismissed their calls for an apology for the atrocities as "self-serving statements by politicians, self-aggrandizement narratives, pompous declarations, and political posturing and propaganda _."_[[331]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-mlLateStrongmanSon-333)[[332]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-enrilesMemoir-334) In the _[Sydney Morning Herald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Morning_Herald "Sydney Morning Herald")_ later that year, Bongbong cited the various court decisions against the Marcos family as a reason not to apologize for Martial Law abuses, saying "we have a judgment against us in the billions. What more would people want?"[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-SydneyMorningHerald20121124-27)
During his 2016 vice presidential campaign, Marcos responded to then-president [Benigno Aquino III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benigno_Aquino_III "Benigno Aquino III")'s criticism of the Marcos regime and call to oppose his election run. He dismissed the events, saying Filipinos should "leave history to the professors."[[333]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-inqLetHistorians-335)[[334]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-gmaLeaveItToProfs-336)[[335]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-absLetHistorians-337) This prompted over 500 faculty, staff and history professors from the [Ateneo de Manila University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ateneo_de_Manila_University "Ateneo de Manila University") to immediately issue a statement condemning his dismissive retort as part of "an ongoing willful distortion of our history," and a "shameless refusal to acknowledge the crimes of the Martial Law regime."[[336]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-AdMUStatement-338)[[337]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-AdMUStatementPDF-339)[[338]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-AteneoPresidents-340)[[339]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-inqAteneoProfsSlam-341)[[340]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-interaksyonAteneoProfsThumbDown-342) More than 1,400 Catholic schools, through the Catholic Educational Association of the Philippines (CEAP), later joined the call of the Ateneo faculty "against the attempt of [Marcos] to canonize the harrowing horrors of martial rule."[[341]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-ceapStatement-343)[[342]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-abs1400-344) This was also followed by the [University of the Philippines Diliman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_Philippines_Diliman "University of the Philippines Diliman")'s Department of History, which released a statement of its own, decrying what they called a "dangerous" effort for Marcos to create "myth and deception."[[343]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-fbUPHistoryDeptStatement-345)[[344]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-inqMarcosDeception-346)[[345]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-PhilStarUpProfsSlam-347)
On September 20, 2018, Marcos Jr. released a YouTube video showing a [tête-à-tête](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/t%C3%AAte-%C3%A0-t%C3%AAte "wiktionary:tête-à-tête") between him and former senate president [Juan Ponce Enrile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Ponce_Enrile "Juan Ponce Enrile"), who had been his father's defense minister before playing a key role in his ouster during the 1986 EDSA revolution.[[346]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-PatriciaLourdesViray20180921-348) The video made a number of claims, which were quickly refuted and denounced by martial law victims, including former senate president [Aquilino Pimentel Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquilino_Pimentel_Jr. "Aquilino Pimentel Jr."), former [DSWD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Social_Welfare_and_Development "Department of Social Welfare and Development") secretary [Judy Taguiwalo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judy_Taguiwalo "Judy Taguiwalo"), former Commission on Human Rights chair [Etta Rosales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etta_Rosales "Etta Rosales"), and writer [Boni Ilagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boni_Ilagan "Boni Ilagan"), among others. Enrile later backpedaled from some of his claims, attributing them to "unlucid intervals."[[347]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-PaoloRomero20181026-349)
### Online presence
According to research by [Vera Files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vera_Files "Vera Files"), Marcos benefited the most from fake news from the Philippines in 2017, along with President Rodrigo Duterte.[[348]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-VeraFiles-2017-350) Most viral news were driven by shares on networks of Facebook pages.[[348]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-VeraFiles-2017-350) Also, most Philippine audience Facebook pages and groups spreading online disinformation bore "Duterte", "Marcos" or "News" in their names and are pro-Duterte.[[349]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-351)
In July 2020, [Brittany Kaiser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brittany_Kaiser "Brittany Kaiser") alleged in an interview that Marcos had approached the controversial firm [Cambridge Analytica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge_Analytica "Cambridge Analytica") in order to "rebrand" the Marcos family image on social media.[[350]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-352) Marcos's spokesperson Vic Rodriguez denied these allegations and stated that Marcos is considering filing libel charges against [Rappler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rappler "Rappler"), which published Kaiser's interview.[[351]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-353)
### Impostor urban legend
Between the late 70s and early 80s, an urban legend became popular claiming that Marcos Jr. was stabbed and died during a scuffle while studying abroad. The Marcos family allegedly looked for Bongbong's look-alike to replace him. This was later debunked by Marcos in one of his vlogs. The origins of this urban legend remain unknown.[[352]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-354)
### Tallano gold myth
See also: [Tallano gold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallano_gold "Tallano gold")
In 1990, during a coverage of Imelda Marcos's trial in New York, [Inquirer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Daily_Inquirer "Philippine Daily Inquirer") journalist Kristina Luz interviewed then-33-year-old exiled Bongbong Marcos and asked where the Marcos wealth came from. Marcos responded "only I know where the gold is and how to get it". This was corroborated in a 1992 report by the [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press") that quoted Imelda Marcos saying that her husband's wealth came "from the Japanese and other gold he found after [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), and not from the Philippine coffers." In 2007, Marcos informed the anti-graft court [Sandiganbayan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandiganbayan "Sandiganbayan") that his [father](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos "Ferdinand Marcos")'s wealth came from trading "precious metals more specifically gold from the years 1946 to 1954" when he tried to win back the [Ortigas Payanig property in Pasig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#2007_Payanig_sa_Pasig_property_case_motion) from the national government.[[353]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-355)
The myth surrounding the gold allegedly owned by the Marcos family has been the subject of various misinformation, as in 2011, a Facebook post claimed that a certain "Tallano clan" had paid Ferdinand Marcos in gold for his legal services. Several years later, supporters of the Marcos family in a Facebook page called "Marcos Cyber Warriors" also claimed that Marcos Sr.'s wealth came from his former law client, the "Maharlikan Tallano family".[[354]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-InqTallano-356)
This has resulted in a long-running belief that should Bongbong Marcos win as president, he will give Filipinos a share of this gold. However during his [Philippine presidential election campaign in the 2022 elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Philippine_presidential_election "2022 Philippine presidential election"), when asked over [One News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_News_\(TV_channel\) "One News \(TV channel\)") to verify the mythical "[Tallano gold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallano_gold "Tallano gold")" or the long-believed tale that they got a share of the Japanese [Yamashita gold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamashita_gold "Yamashita gold"), Marcos denied knowledge of it, even joking that "people should let him know if they see any of that gold". The urban myth had allegedly been suggested or carried by various social media pages being run by Marcos supporters in order to engage more people to support his presidential bid.[[354]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-InqTallano-356)

Marcos is married to lawyer [Louise "Liza" Cacho Araneta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louise_Araneta%E2%80%93Marcos "Louise Araneta–Marcos"), a member of the prominent [Araneta family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Araneta_family "Araneta family"). Aside from his common nickname "Bongbong", Marcos is known by his peers as "Bonggets".[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Geronimo20151012-43) Marcos is an avid listener of [rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll"), [rhythm and blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_and_blues "Rhythm and blues"), and [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz") music. He once held a [record collection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_collecting "Record collecting") in Malacañang Palace that he described as "the best record collection in the Philippines" but left it when his family was exiled from the country in 1986. He is a fan of [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles"), citing _[Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sgt._Pepper's_Lonely_Hearts_Club_Band "Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band")_ as his favorite album of theirs, and often collects [the band's memorabilia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_impact_of_the_Beatles "Cultural impact of the Beatles"). Marcos can also play the saxophone.[[361]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-The_other_side_of_Bongbong-363)
Marcos exercises regularly and claims to abstain from consuming confections and soft drinks,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Geronimo20151012-43) and also enjoys cooking.[[362]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-How_Marcos_learned_about_home-cooked_dishes-364) Marcos is also an avid reader, a [cinephile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinephile "Cinephile"), and a gun enthusiast, where he holds a competition under his name.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Geronimo20151012-43)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-25_things-49)[[363]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Filipino_politicians,_guns,_and_power-365) Marcos also follows [Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One") racing as a supporter of [Scuderia Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari"); during his presidency, he attended the [2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Singapore_Grand_Prix "2022 Singapore Grand Prix"), [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Singapore_Grand_Prix "2023 Singapore Grand Prix"),[[364]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-366)[[365]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-Marcos_back_in_PH_on_Sunday,_says_Palace-367) and [2026 Singapore Grands Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Singapore_Grand_Prix "2026 Singapore Grand Prix").[[366]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-368)
On March 31, 2020, Marcos's spokesperson confirmed that Marcos had tested positive for [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_in_the_Philippines "COVID-19 in the Philippines").[[367]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-tests-positive-covid-19-369) Prior to getting tested, Marcos was reportedly experiencing chest pains after coming home from a trip to Spain. He has since recovered from the disease after testing negative on a [RT-PCR test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_testing#Reverse_transcription_polymerase_chain_reaction_\(RT-PCR\)_test "COVID-19 testing") on May 5, 2020, a month after testing positive for COVID-19.[[368]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-recovery-covid-19-370) On July 8, 2022, Marcos's press secretary confirmed that Marcos had tested positive again for COVID-19 after experiencing slight fever.[[369]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-371)
In January 2026, Marcos was diagnosed with [diverticulitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diverticulitis "Diverticulitis").[[370]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-372)
### Alleged cocaine usage
On November 18, 2021, President [Rodrigo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte "Rodrigo Duterte") claimed in a televised speech that a certain candidate for the [2022 Philippine presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Philippine_presidential_election "2022 Philippine presidential election") is allegedly using [cocaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocaine "Cocaine"), hinting at the candidate using male pronouns on several instances. Furthermore, Duterte alleged that the candidate eluded law enforcement authorities by doing drugs on a private yacht and a plane.[[371]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-373) Although he did not name the candidate, it was alluded that Duterte was referring to Marcos after he continued on his speech that the male candidate is a "weak leader" and has been "capitalizing on [his father](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos "Ferdinand Marcos")'s accomplishments".[[372]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-374) Prior to that, Duterte previously named Marcos a "weak leader who had done nothing" and a "spoiled child for being an only son".[[373]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-375)
Days after Duterte's allegation, Marcos took a cocaine [drug test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_test "Drug test") through a urine sample at [St. Luke's Medical Center – Global City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Luke's_Medical_Center_%E2%80%93_Global_City "St. Luke's Medical Center – Global City") and submitted the negative result to law enforcement authorities with a follow-up online memo by the medical institution confirming the legitimacy of the test.[[374]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-376)
Marcos responded that he did not feel that he was the one alluded to by President Duterte. According to [health care provider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_care_provider "Health care provider") [American Addiction Centers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Addiction_Centers "American Addiction Centers"), after the last use, cocaine or its metabolites can show up on a blood or saliva test for up to two days, a urine test for up to three days, and a hair test for months to years.[[375]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-377) In an interview with [CNN Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN_Philippines "CNN Philippines") in April 2022, Marcos responded to Duterte's remarks on him being a "spoiled" and "weak leader", saying that the president was "playing politics" and was "always making sure everybody's thinking hard about what they're doing".[[376]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-378)
In an interview with [ANC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABS-CBN_News_Channel "ABS-CBN News Channel") in May 2022, former senator [Nikki Coseteng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Coseteng "Nikki Coseteng"), who claimed to personally know Marcos, alleged that Marcos was a "lazy individual" who frequented [discos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nightclub "Nightclub") and got high on illegal substances along with his socialite friends during his youth.[[377]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-379) Marcos has neither denied nor confirmed Coseteng's allegations.[[378]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-380)
In late January 2024, Marcos's alleged cocaine use was brought anew by Duterte, during a prayer rally against [Charter change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_reform_in_the_Philippines "Constitutional reform in the Philippines") in [Davao City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davao_City "Davao City").[[379]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-fentanyl-381) Duterte alleged that Marcos had once been included in the [Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Drug_Enforcement_Agency "Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency")'s (PDEA) drug watchlist (which the agency denied) and had been spotted using cocaine with his cohorts at a giant banana firm's plantation in [Davao del Norte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davao_del_Norte "Davao del Norte") when Duterte was Mayor. Duterte said that these companions of Marcos were already working for his administration, and cited this as the reason why he did not vote for him in the 2022 general election. When asked by Marcos to prove the allegations, Duterte retorted that it is incumbent upon him to prove the allegations by taking a drug test, since he is the one holding public office.[[379]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-fentanyl-381) Marcos maintained he had never used illegal narcotics, let alone cocaine, and blamed Duterte's use of [fentanyl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fentanyl "Fentanyl") as a response. In Duterte's defense, he had used fentanyl because it was prescribed to him by a "Dr. Javier", his alleged physician at [St. Luke's Medical Center – Quezon City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Luke's_Medical_Center_%E2%80%93_Quezon_City "St. Luke's Medical Center – Quezon City"), to alleviate pain from injuries sustained in a motorbike accident a few years ago.[[379]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-fentanyl-381)
In April 2024, leaked documents from the [Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Drug_Enforcement_Agency "Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency") (PDEA) circulated online, linking Marcos and actress [Maricel Soriano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maricel_Soriano "Maricel Soriano") to illegal drugs. The [Senate Committee on Public Order and Dangerous Drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Senate_Committee_on_Public_Order_and_Dangerous_Drugs "Philippine Senate Committee on Public Order and Dangerous Drugs"), headed by Senator [Ronald dela Rosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_dela_Rosa "Ronald dela Rosa"), later conducted a hearing on the matter and invited vlogger Maharlika to explain her involvement in the online circulation of the documents. Former PDEA investigation agent Jonathan Morales declared that the documents were authentic; PDEA Director General Moro Virgilio Lazo, on the other hand, claimed the documents were fake.[[380]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-382)
On May 20, 2024, the [Philippine Senate Committee on Public Order and Dangerous Drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Senate_Committee_on_Public_Order_and_Dangerous_Drugs "Philippine Senate Committee on Public Order and Dangerous Drugs") panel cited [PDEA agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Drug_Enforcement_Agency "Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency") Jonathan Morales in [contempt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contempt_of_court "Contempt of court") for '["continuously lying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perjury "Perjury")". Upon [Jinggoy Estrada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinggoy_Estrada "Jinggoy Estrada")'s [motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_\(parliamentary_procedure\) "Motion \(parliamentary procedure\)") and [seconded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_\(parliamentary_procedure\) "Second \(parliamentary procedure\)") by [Ronald dela Rosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_dela_Rosa "Ronald dela Rosa"), Morales was ordered [detained](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preventive_detention "Preventive detention") for [flipped-flopped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip-flop_\(politics\) "Flip-flop \(politics\)") replies on [PDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_data "Personal data"), inter alia. Earlier, a former [National Police Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Police_Commission_\(Philippines\) "National Police Commission \(Philippines\)") officer, Eric "Pikoy" Santiago was also held in contempt of the Senate for being a "liar".[[381]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-383)[[382]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-384) On May 23, 2024, Morales and Santiago were released from custody according to [Senate Sergeant-at-Arms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serjeant-at-arms "Serjeant-at-arms") Roberto Ancan.[[383]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-385) In August 2024, [San Fernando, Pampanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Fernando,_Pampanga "San Fernando, Pampanga") Municipal Trial Court Branch 9 Acting Presiding Judge Jason Alquiroz convicted Morales of [perjury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perjury "Perjury") and sentenced him to four months [imprisonment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imprisonment "Imprisonment") and fined ₱1,000.[[384]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-386)
In November 2025, Marcos' sister [Imee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imee_Marcos "Imee Marcos") alleged that their family knew about Marcos' use of illegal drugs, stating during a three-day [Iglesia ni Cristo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iglesia_ni_Cristo "Iglesia ni Cristo") rally in [Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila "Manila") that "when Bongbong and I were still kids, the whole family already knew about his problem. In truth, the testimonies of my father regarding his attitude and actions can be read by everyone. Before, he was not my responsibility because we still had a father. Growing up, [he] became more concerning."[[385]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos#cite_note-387)
